infinite_horizon.handbook.phase_1.elektr: The <item:infinite_horizon:electrolyzer> uses power to split water into **hydrogen** and **oxygen**. You will urgently need both later: hydrogen as fuel, oxygen for breathing on alien worlds.
Put a <item:infinite_horizon:fluid_pump> above water, or put water buckets into the drain slot.
Lead the water with a <item:infinite_horizon:copper_pipe> to any side of the electrolyzer.
The gases come out through the **output side**. The "Tank" button chooses which gas the fill slot takes.
Gases fit neither in the normal tank nor in buckets. For now they collect in the electrolyzer itself. Pressure bottles and canisters come in a later phase.

The <item:infinite_horizon:electric_furnace> smelts everything a normal furnace smelts, but uses power instead of fuel. It can also do things no furnace can, for example <item:infinite_horizon:silicon> from quartz sand.
The electric furnace takes the same time for every recipe and gives no experience. It cannot do blast furnace or smoker recipes.
The electric furnace accepts every vanilla smelting recipe. That includes the ingots from Infinite Horizon:
infinite_horizon.handbook.phase_1.erste_: In the first phase you build a small industry on Earth. By the end you have power, process ores twice as efficiently as in a furnace, make circuits and refine crude oil into kerosene and plastic. That is the foundation for everything that follows.

**Gather resources.** Above all you need iron, copper and redstone. Also look out for <item:infinite_horizon:bauxite_ore> in savanna, desert and badlands, and for <item:infinite_horizon:titanium_ore> deep underground. More under [[infinite_horizon:phase_1/rohstoffe|Resources and Ores]].
**Build machine frames.** Almost every machine needs a <item:infinite_horizon:machine_frame>. Build two or three right away.
**Split water.** The <item:infinite_horizon:electrolyzer> turns water into hydrogen and oxygen. See [[infinite_horizon:phase_1/elektrolyseur|Electrolyzer]].
**Get faster.** With circuits you build [[infinite_horizon:phase_1/upgrades|upgrades]] that speed up your machines or make them more efficient.

**Generate power.** A <item:infinite_horizon:combustion_generator> burns coal or wood and supplies power. Connect it to your machines with <item:infinite_horizon:copper_cable>. See [[infinite_horizon:phase_1/strom|Power]].

**Double your ores.** The <item:infinite_horizon:crusher> turns one raw ore into two dusts. Smelt the dust in a furnace or in the <item:infinite_horizon:electric_furnace>. See [[infinite_horizon:phase_1/zerkleinerer|Crusher]].
**Press plates, rods and wire.** The <item:infinite_horizon:press> reshapes ingots with a mold. You will constantly need copper wire and iron plates. See [[infinite_horizon:phase_1/presse|Press]].
**Smelt silicon.** <item:infinite_horizon:quartz_sand> from beaches or river banks becomes <item:infinite_horizon:silicon> in the electric furnace.
**Build the assembly table.** From now on all important components come out of the <item:infinite_horizon:assembly_table>. See [[infinite_horizon:phase_1/montagetisch|Assembly Table]].

**Pump crude oil.** Oil pockets lie under deserts and oceans. A <item:infinite_horizon:fluid_pump> sucks the crude oil into a <item:infinite_horizon:fluid_tank>. See [[infinite_horizon:phase_1/fluide|Fluids and Pipes]].
**Build the refinery.** The first multiblock turns crude oil into kerosene and plastic. See [[infinite_horizon:phase_1/raffinerie|Refinery]].
**Make circuits.** Silicon, copper wire and plastic give the <item:infinite_horizon:circuit> in the assembly table, the most important component of the mod.
Crush your ores instead of smelting them directly. One raw ore then gives two ingots. That pays off from day one.
infinite_horizon.handbook.phase_1.fluide: Crude oil, kerosene, hydrogen and oxygen are **fluids**. They are measured in millibuckets: 1,000 mB are one bucket.

The <item:infinite_horizon:fluid_tank> holds 16,000 mB of one liquid. It outputs only through its output side and keeps its contents when you break it. Gases do not fit; for now they stay in the machine's tank.
Every machine with a tank has two special slots:
**Fill slot:** put an empty bucket in, and the machine fills it from its tank.
**Drain slot:** put a full bucket in, and the machine empties it into its tank.
You also get a Crude Oil Bucket by clicking a crude oil source block with an empty bucket. A <item:infinite_horizon:kerosene_bucket> can only be filled in the fill slot of the refinery or a tank.
Put the pump directly above an oil pocket and the tank next to it. With a copper pipe in between, the crude oil flows by itself.

The <item:infinite_horizon:fluid_pump> drains source blocks below it: water, lava or crude oil, up to 8 blocks deep and the same distance to the sides. Each operation brings 1,000 mB. With crude oil, the source block disappears only with 10 % probability, so an oil pocket lasts a very long time.
A pipe that already carries water does not accept crude oil. If nothing flows, check whether an old fluid is still stuck in the network.
The <item:infinite_horizon:copper_pipe> carries liquids and gases, 200 mB per tick. Two important rules:
A pipe network always carries **only one fluid**. Only once it is empty can another one enter. So water and crude oil need separate pipes.
Pipes never pull by themselves. Machines and tanks **push** their output in through their output side.
infinite_horizon.handbook.phase_1.montag: The <item:infinite_horizon:assembly_table> is the heart of your workshop. Almost everything after the first phase is made here: circuits, machines, rocket parts, space suits.
The assembly table has **9 input slots** without a fixed pattern, a fluid tank and 3 output slots.
The <item:infinite_horizon:circuit> goes into almost every machine from phase 2 on. Set up a small production for it early.
If the arrow does not start although everything seems to be there: take everything out and put the ingredients back in exactly the recipe amounts.
The assembly table is picky: a recipe only starts if the slots hold **exactly** the ingredients in **exactly** the right amount. If a slot holds a little too much or something else, nothing happens.
One ingredient may occupy several slots. The amounts are added up.
Exactly the amount from the recipe is used.

Example: 4 <item:infinite_horizon:iron_plate> and 1 <item:infinite_horizon:copper_pipe> give a <item:infinite_horizon:fluid_port>. With 2 plates and 1 pipe you get <item:infinite_horizon:refinery_casing> instead.
infinite_horizon.handbook.phase_1.presse: The <item:infinite_horizon:press> reshapes ingots. The **mold** in the mold slot decides which shape comes out. The mold is not used up.

Build several presses and run each with its own mold. Then you never have to swap the mold. You need <item:infinite_horizon:copper_wire> and <item:infinite_horizon:iron_plate> in particular in large amounts.
infinite_horizon.handbook.phase_1.raffin: The refinery is your first **multiblock**: a tower of 45 blocks that turns crude oil into **kerosene** and **plastic**. Kerosene is fuel, and plastic goes into every circuit.
Ports replace casing blocks and pass things on to the controller. Right-clicking with an empty hand switches between **input** and **output**.
For 44 casing blocks you need 11 assembly runs, that is 22 iron plates and 11 copper pipes. Every port saves you one casing block.
Other blocks are not allowed in the structure. Even a single wrong block makes the lamp glow red. Hover over the lamp in the window: it shows the first missing block with its coordinates.
The refinery is **3 blocks wide, 3 blocks deep and 5 blocks tall**, completely solid.
Place the controller (<item:infinite_horizon:refinery_controller>) on the ground. Its front faces you.
The controller is the **middle of the bottom row on the front**. The tower extends one block left and right of it, two blocks back and four blocks up.
Replace single casing blocks with **ports** where pipes and cables should connect (see below).
As soon as everything is right, the status lamp turns from red to yellow.
**Sneak-right-click** the controller with an empty hand to see, for 200 t (10 s), red particles where blocks are missing or wrong.
infinite_horizon.handbook.phase_1.rohsto: Besides the vanilla ores, Infinite Horizon brings three new resources to Earth. On top of that there is crude oil deep in the ground.

Crude oil sits in **oil pockets** under deserts and oceans, between y -20 and 40. About one in 8 chunks has one. You see nothing of it at the surface; you often find one when a cave suddenly gleams black. How to pump crude oil is explained under [[infinite_horizon:phase_1/fluide|Fluids and Pipes]].
You can smelt bauxite directly in a furnace. If you crush it first, though, you get twice as much aluminium.
6 veins per chunk, up to 12 blocks each
4 veins per chunk, up to 6 blocks each

<item:infinite_horizon:bauxite> is the raw form of aluminium. You find it high up, between y 50 and 120, but only in hot, dry areas: savanna, desert and badlands. A stone pickaxe is enough to mine it.

<item:infinite_horizon:titanium_ore> lies deep in the ground, below y 0 mostly as the deepslate variant. You need at least an **iron pickaxe**, otherwise you get nothing. You will need titanium for rockets in large amounts, so remember good spots.
<item:infinite_horizon:quartz_sand> lies in small disks on beaches and river banks, much like clay. The electric furnace turns it into <item:infinite_horizon:silicon>.
All machines run on power, measured in **joules (J)**. How much a machine needs per tick is shown as **J/t** on its page. One tick is a twentieth of a second.

<item:infinite_horizon:copper_cable> connects by itself to everything that produces or needs power. A cable network carries at most 256 J/t, no matter how long it is. Generators push their power out of all sides, and the network spreads it evenly over all machines.

The <item:infinite_horizon:battery> stores power for the night or for load peaks. It accepts power on all sides and outputs it only through its **output side** (button "Side" in the window). That way it can cleanly separate two networks.
A copper cable network carries 256 J/t. If that is not enough, split your machines into several networks, each with its own generator.
Machines only use power while they work. If power runs short, they pause and later continue where they left off. Nothing is lost.
The <item:infinite_horizon:combustion_generator> is your first power plant. It burns anything that burns in a furnace and supplies 20 J/t. Lava buckets work too; the empty bucket stays in the slot.
anything that burns in a furnace (e.g. Coal: 1,600 t (80 s))
Once your [[infinite_horizon:phase_1/raffinerie|refinery]] runs, the <item:infinite_horizon:fuel_generator> is worth it. It burns kerosene and supplies 80 J/t – many times the combustion generator.
infinite_horizon.handbook.phase_1.upgrad: Every machine has two upgrade slots at the bottom right. Generators and storage blocks have none.
**Slot 1:** <item:infinite_horizon:speed_upgrade> – each operation takes only 0.75 times as long, but uses 1.5 times the power per tick.
**Slot 2:** <item:infinite_horizon:efficiency_upgrade> – lowers power use per tick to 0.85 times.
Each slot takes up to 4 upgrades. The effects multiply: four speed upgrades make a crusher more than three times as fast.
Combine both: speed upgrades for more pace, efficiency upgrades so your cable network does not get overloaded.
You can insert and remove upgrades at any time. A running operation keeps its progress.
infinite_horizon.handbook.phase_1.zerkle: The <item:infinite_horizon:crusher> is the first machine you should build. It grinds the raw forms of metals into **two** dusts. Smelt the dust and every ore gives you two ingots instead of one.
Put a hopper on top of the crusher and a second one below it into an electric furnace. Then raw ore turns into ingots all by itself.
You smelt dust in a normal furnace or in the [[infinite_horizon:phase_1/elektroofen|electric furnace]]:
You get the <item:infinite_horizon:planetary_atlas> as a gift on your first login. **Right-click** opens it. What it contains belongs to your agency: all members see the same atlas.
On the left are all destinations, ordered by their distance from the Sun. On the right you see for the selected destination:
**Discoverer:** the first agency whose member set foot on the destination. Whoever arrives first is announced to all players.
**Environment values**, as soon as a probe has arrived: gravity, temperature by day and night, pressure and radiation.
**Visited biomes:** they count as soon as a member travels there.
**Exploration targets** with coordinates, e.g. the lava tubes on the [[infinite_horizon:phase_2/mond|Moon]].
**Landing beacons** of your agency, see [[infinite_horizon:phase_3/landefeuer|The Landing Beacon]].
Lost it? You craft a new atlas at the crafting table. It immediately shows everything your agency knows again.
infinite_horizon.handbook.phase_2.erste_: In the second phase you leave Earth. The goal is the Moon: new resources wait there, but also the first real dangers.
**Set up the research terminal.** It opens research tier 1, see [[infinite_horizon:phase_2/forschung|Research]].
**Collect research points.** Take samples of ores with the <item:infinite_horizon:sample_tool> and evaluate them in the <item:infinite_horizon:analyzer>. Research the pressure suit first.
**Send a probe to the Moon.** Build a [[infinite_horizon:phase_2/raumfahrt|launch pad]] with fuel pump and control panel and launch a probe. Only once it has arrived is the Moon a rocket destination.
**Build and fuel the rocket.** Engine, fins, tanks and capsule on the pad, kerosene and oxygen into the pump, see [[infinite_horizon:phase_2/rakete|The Rocket]].
**Know the dangers.** Read what awaits you on alien worlds: [[infinite_horizon:start/umwelt|Environment, Strain and Gravity]].

**Fly to the Moon.** Sit in the capsule wearing your suit, open the rocket computer with the inventory key and press "Launch". On the navigation map you choose the Moon and the landing site, see [[infinite_horizon:phase_2/flug|The Flight]].

**Explore the Moon.** Highlands, mare and craters have their own ores, and research points wait in the lava tubes of the mare. See [[infinite_horizon:phase_2/mond|The Moon]]. [[infinite_horizon:phase_2/strom_im_all|Solar panels]] supply power there.

**Fill the atlas.** The [[infinite_horizon:phase_2/atlas|planetary atlas]] shows which biomes and exploration targets your agency already knows. A helmet lamp in the [[infinite_horizon:phase_2/raumanzug|pressure suit]] helps in dark craters.
Set up a [[infinite_horizon:phase_3/landefeuer|landing beacon]] at your base before you take off. Then the return flight brings you home instead of to world spawn.
infinite_horizon.handbook.phase_2.flug.e: Once the [[infinite_horizon:phase_2/rakete|rocket]] stands fuelled on the [[infinite_horizon:phase_2/raumfahrt|launch pad]] and every point of the checklist is met, you are ready to go.
Launching
**Get out:** sneak.
**Get in:** right-click while a seat is free.

**Rocket GUI:** inventory key in the seat or right-click from outside. There you see the fuel, the cargo hold and the buttons **Launch** and **Refuel**. Refuel empties <item:infinite_horizon:transport_tank> from the cargo hold into the rocket tanks.
**Dismantle:** sneak and right-click with an empty hand. All parts and the cargo drop as items, the fuel is lost.
The return flight

A landed rocket launches without a pad: sit down, open the rocket GUI and press **Launch**. The cost depends on the gravity of the launch site; from the Moon the return flight is much cheaper than the outbound one.
You reach yellow destinations only once. Without fuel in the cargo hold or a pump at the destination you are stuck there.
Set up a [[infinite_horizon:phase_3/landefeuer|landing beacon]] at your base on Earth before the first flight. Then the return flight lands you at home instead of world spawn.
Put on the complete [[infinite_horizon:phase_2/raumanzug|pressure suit]] and take enough [[infinite_horizon:phase_2/sauerstoff|oxygen canisters]].
Sit down in the capsule (right-click the capsule).
Press the **inventory key**. In the seat it opens the rocket computer of the control panel. You can also open the panel from outside.
When the checklist is complete, press **Launch**. The **navigation map** opens.
On the left are the destinations with their fuel cost there and back: **green** means there and back, **yellow** one way only, **grey** locked or too far. Choose a destination.

On the right you choose the landing site: a [[infinite_horizon:phase_3/landefeuer|landing beacon]] of your agency on that body, or your own X and Z coordinates. If you leave both empty, you land at the destination's spawn (on Earth at world spawn, elsewhere near X/Z 0/0).
Press **Launch**. The rocket's blocks become a flying rocket with all passengers inside.
The flight
**Countdown:** 200 t (10 s). From now on you cannot get out.
**Ascent:** 600 t (30 s) straight up. The camera shows the rocket from outside.
**Arrival:** 200 blocks above the landing point (at most up to the build height).
**Landing:** 200 t (10 s), then the rocket stands on the highest solid block.
Press **Esc** to skip the flight: the rocket lands at the destination immediately.
The rocket searches for a landing spot in a spiral within 32 blocks: solid ground without liquid and 3 blocks of air above.
If you log out during the flight, the rocket lands immediately. At your next login you are sitting in it again.
After landing
The rocket stays as a vehicle.
infinite_horizon.handbook.phase_2.forsch: Research starts your space program. At the <item:infinite_horizon:research_terminal> your [[infinite_horizon:reference/agentur|agency]] spends **research points (RP)** to unlock new components and destinations. Research belongs to the whole agency: what one member researches, everyone can build.

A node unlocks **all recipes** whose result it names. As long as your agency has not researched it, your machines and your assembly table do not make those things: the status lamp stays yellow and its tooltip says "Locked". Anything not listed in a node can always be made, for example circuits, upgrades, ports, the terminal itself and the probe.
That also affects ten things you may already have built:
Blocks already built and finished suits keep working. Only crafting is locked.
You need the pressure suit for the first trip to the Moon. Research the **Pressure suit** node early, otherwise your assembly table builds no new suit parts.
RP belong to the agency and are shown with two decimal places. You get them in two ways: from **samples** evaluated by the analyzer, and from **exploration targets**.
Right-clicking a block gives a <item:infinite_horizon:sample>. The block stays where it is. Afterwards the tool needs a 40 t (2 s) break.
Every spot gives only one sample. Blocks placed by a player never give one: the action bar then says "No usable sample".
Build the terminal at the assembly table (recipe below) and place it in your base. It needs no power.
As soon as it stands, research **tier 1** opens for your agency, and you get the advancement "Ground Station".

Right-click opens the **research tree**: four columns for the branches industry and energy, spaceflight, life support and logistics, six rows for the tiers. Drag the area with the mouse and scroll it (with Shift horizontally).
Your agency's RP are shown at the top right.

On Earth only ores can be sampled: <item:infinite_horizon:bauxite_ore>, <item:infinite_horizon:titanium_ore>, <item:infinite_horizon:quartz_sand> and the vanilla ores coal, iron, copper, gold, redstone, lapis and diamond. Deepslate variants count as the normal ore. On the [[infinite_horizon:phase_2/mond|Moon]] every natural Moon block gives a sample. Samples from the Nether and the End are worthless.

The <item:infinite_horizon:analyzer> evaluates one sample per operation and credits the RP to your agency. It needs power and only accepts samples that give RP. An analyzer that belongs to nobody does not work (red lamp), so place it yourself.
For every **sample kind** (block and location) the first 10 samples count in full, every further one only 10 %. On Earth you can collect up to 100 RP at full value this way.

When a member enters a **lava tube** on the Moon, the agency gets 20 RP, once per tube. Lava tubes are straight tunnels deep in the mare, between y 30 and 50. Here, too, the first 10 finds count in full.
On servers, mandatory research can be switched off (setting `research_required`). Then all recipes and handbook chapters are open, and the tree shows a notice.
Every node shows its icon with a coloured frame:
Set up the terminal right at the start. It only costs material, opens tier 1 and shows you in the tree what comes next.
Take a sample of every ore you find while mining. Samples of many different ore kinds bring more than many samples of the same kind.
locked: tier still closed or a prerequisite is missing
The tooltip lists the cost, what it unlocks and missing prerequisites. Researching deducts the RP right away. Leaders and engineers of the agency may research.

A tier opens when the previous one is open and its **gate** is met. Open tiers never close again, even if you break the terminal. The row headers in the tree show each gate and a check mark once the tier is open.
a member sets foot on the Moon
magnesium and tungsten ingots and helium made
a zero-g fabricator of the agency finishes an operation
The tiers also open the chapters of this handbook: you can read the third phase ("Ring 1") from tier 2.
infinite_horizon.handbook.phase_2.mond.e: The Moon is the first destination of your space program. It is close but hostile: no air, vacuum and strong temperature swings between day and night. In return, aluminium and titanium lie here in large amounts.
At night and in the dark, zombies, skeletons, spiders and creepers show up, but less often than on Earth. They wear breathing masks and need no oxygen.
Without protection you survive on the Moon only for seconds: oxygen, pressure and temperature build up strain immediately.
Land at night or at dusk if you can. It is cold then, but you are spared the midday heat of 120 °C.
**Gravity:** 0.17 times Earth's. You jump higher and fall more gently (see [[infinite_horizon:start/umwelt|Environment, Strain and Gravity]]).
**Temperature:** 120 °C at noon, -170 °C at night. Always -190 °C in the polar crater.
**Sky:** black, the stars shine even by day, and Earth hangs large in the sky.
**Day and night** run as on Earth.
**Moon Mare:** flat, dark plains of <item:infinite_horizon:moon_basalt>. The lava tubes run here too, long straight tunnels deep in the rock.
**Moon Great Crater:** home of the great craters with a central peak. Inside them you find twice as much ore.
**Moon Polar Crater:** rare and freezing cold, with patches of <item:infinite_horizon:moon_ice>. There is no solar power here.
Small craters are scattered everywhere. Below the surface the Moon consists of <item:infinite_horizon:moon_rock>.
3 veins per chunk, up to 6 blocks each
5 veins per chunk, up to 8 blocks each
4 veins per chunk, up to 6 blocks each
4 veins per chunk, up to 16 blocks each

<item:infinite_horizon:moon_aluminum_ore> needs at least a stone pickaxe, <item:infinite_horizon:moon_titanium_ore> an iron pickaxe, just as on Earth. <item:infinite_horizon:moon_ice> drops ordinary ice when mined.
infinite_horizon.handbook.phase_2.rakete: You build a rocket block by block on the [[infinite_horizon:phase_2/raumfahrt|launch pad]]. Every part is one block in size.
The rocket computer in the control panel works this out for every destination: **green** means there and back, **yellow** one way only, **grey** unreachable or no probe yet.
The control panel lists these points, which all need a check mark:
**Structure valid:** pad and rocket are built correctly (e.g. all fins at the engine).
**Destination unlocked:** Earth and every destination a probe of your agency has reached.
**Crew:** a player in a complete [[infinite_horizon:phase_2/raumanzug|pressure suit]] sits in the capsule.
How launch, flight and landing work is explained under [[infinite_horizon:phase_2/flug|The Flight]].
Plan the return flight: you can reach yellow destinations, but you will not get back without refuelling. Take fuel in the cargo bay or build a pump at the destination.
For the Moon even the smallest rocket with full tanks is enough for the round trip. More tanks bring reserves, but also weight.
From bottom to top above the centre of the platform:
4 <item:infinite_horizon:rocket_fin_t1> horizontally next to the engine, one each to the north, east, south and west.
3 to 5 <item:infinite_horizon:rocket_tank_t1> stacked on top of each other.
If you like, a <item:infinite_horizon:rocket_cargo_bay> for cargo (27 slots, right-click opens it).
At the very top the <item:infinite_horizon:rocket_capsule_t1>. Right-clicking it seats you inside, sneaking lets you get out.
The T1 engine has a thrust of 30. The rocket may only launch if **thrust / (mass × gravity)** is at least 1. Many full tanks plus a full cargo bay are too heavy: the rocket computer shows the ratio.
Every tank holds 16,000 mB of kerosene **and** 16,000 mB of oxygen. A flight costs the same amount of both:
**Launch:** 32,000 mB times the gravity of the launch site,
**Transfer:** 6,000 mB per distance point of difference, plus 2,000 mB if the destination is another body,
**Landing:** 25 % of the launch cost at the destination (nothing on Earth).
infinite_horizon.handbook.phase_2.rauman: Without a suit you survive on the Moon only for seconds. The **pressure suit** is the first tier and protects you from vacuum, heat and cold as long as it has oxygen.
Four pieces, one suit

In a vacuum without a dome you hear your breathing and faint radio static. All other sounds are muffled to only 15 % of their volume: footsteps, machines, creatures. The suit's warning tones stay loud.
If it suddenly gets loud around you, you have stepped into a dome. There you breathe freely, and the suit refills.
Modules
Every suit piece has 2 module slots. Modules are installed and removed in the <item:infinite_horizon:assembly_table>, which needs power for this like for any other recipe:
**Install:** put the suit piece and the matching module alone into the inputs. Out comes the piece with the module installed.
**Remove:** put the suit piece in alone. Out come the piece without modules and all modules in the secondary outputs.
Installed modules are listed in the piece's tooltip and stay when you upgrade to a higher suit tier.

**Helmet lamp:** the <item:infinite_horizon:helmet_lamp> goes into the helmet. As long as you wear it, there is light at your head with light level 14, even under water. Take the helmet off and the light is gone.
Crafting
Your agency can only craft the suit pieces once it has researched the **Pressure suit** node (tier 1, [[infinite_horizon:phase_2/forschung|Research]]).

The suit only works if you wear **all four pieces**: <item:infinite_horizon:pressure_suit_helmet>, <item:infinite_horizon:pressure_suit_chestplate>, <item:infinite_horizon:pressure_suit_leggings> and <item:infinite_horizon:pressure_suit_boots>. If one piece is missing, you are unprotected.
Always take one full canister more than you think you need. Do the maths: 600 mB in one canister, 1 mB used every 20 t (1 s).
Protection
Pressure suit
Temperature

vacuum to normal
Radiation

Armor

You repair the suit at an anvil with <item:infinite_horizon:aluminum_plate>.
The oxygen supply
The chestplate holds up to 1,200 mB of oxygen. A new chestplate is empty. Its tooltip shows how much is left and, as soon as you are outside, a bar in the HUD.
**Use:** 1 mB every 20 t (1 s), but only outside breathable air.
**Refilling:** if you wear the chestplate and carry an [[infinite_horizon:phase_2/sauerstoff|oxygen canister]], the supply refills by itself from the first canister.
**Under water** the suit keeps your air full as long as it has oxygen.
When the oxygen is used up, the suit still protects you from pressure and temperature, but you suffocate. Keep an eye on the display.

infinite_horizon.handbook.phase_2.raumfa: Before people fly, a probe flies. Only once it has reached a destination does your agency know the way there, and you can follow with the [[infinite_horizon:phase_2/rakete|rocket]]. Both launch from the same **launch pad**.
Building the launch pad
Research the **Moon probe** node ([[infinite_horizon:phase_2/forschung|Research]]). It makes the Moon a probe destination.
Place a <item:infinite_horizon:probe> on the centre of the pad.
Open the control panel. Under "Probe on the pad" there is a button for every researched destination. One click starts the 200 t (10 s) countdown.
The probe rises and disappears. Its flight takes 1,200 t (60 s) plus 1,200 t (60 s) per distance point of the destination. It keeps going even if you log out.
When it arrives, all members get a message and the advancement "First Signal", and the first time your agency gets 10 RP. From now on the destination is a rocket destination.
A probe never returns. You need a separate one for every destination.
Crafting
Build the tower tall enough for the biggest rocket of your tier right away. Then you do not have to rebuild later.
Platform

<item:infinite_horizon:launch_tower> next to the edge, at least as tall as the rocket

**Platform:** lay an area of <item:infinite_horizon:launch_pad>, 5 × 5 blocks at the same height. Its centre is the block where the engine or the probe will later stand. Additional pad blocks next to it do no harm.

**Tower:** place a vertical column of <item:infinite_horizon:launch_tower> directly next to the edge of the area, not at a corner. Its lowest block stands at platform height. The tower must be at least as tall as the rocket (fins do not count); for a probe one block is enough.
**Pump:** at least one <item:infinite_horizon:fuel_pump> touches the platform or tower with one face.
**Control panel:** place the <item:infinite_horizon:launch_control> at most 8 blocks from the centre. It always controls the nearest valid pad.
The control panel checks the pad when you open it, at launch and every 100 t (5 s). If something is wrong, its lamp glows red and the checklist names the first error.
Fuelling

The fuel pump has two tanks: one for fuel (Kerosene) and one for oxygen. It accepts from all sides, from pipes, tanks and a <item:infinite_horizon:pressure_bottle>, and through the fill and drain slots also from a <item:infinite_horizon:transport_tank>. It needs no power.
