infinite_horizon.handbook.phase_2.sauers: Oxygen is made in the <item:infinite_horizon:electrolyzer> or the [[infinite_horizon:phase_3/sauerstoffgenerator|oxygen generator]]. Canisters and pressure bottles let you carry and store it.
The **Pressure suit** node unlocks the canisters, the **Gas storage** node the pressure bottle (both tier 1, [[infinite_horizon:phase_2/forschung|Research]]).
A pressure bottle next to the oxygen generator collects its surplus. Then you always have a supply for new canisters.
**Filling:** put a canister into the **fill slot** of a machine with an oxygen tank, such as the electrolyzer, oxygen generator or pressure bottle. It fills at once with as much as there is.
**Emptying:** in the **drain slot** the canister empties its contents into the tank.
**On the go:** canisters in your inventory refill your [[infinite_horizon:phase_2/raumanzug|pressure suit]] by themselves.
The tooltip shows the contents. Canisters only take oxygen.
The <item:infinite_horizon:pressure_bottle> is a tank for gases only and holds 8,000 mB. Like the fluid tank it has an output side and fill and drain slots. When broken, it keeps its contents.

The <item:infinite_horizon:transport_tank> is a container for any fluid and holds 16,000 mB, but only one fluid at a time. It works in all fill and drain slots, including the [[infinite_horizon:phase_2/raumfahrt|fuel pump]]. That way you bring kerosene or oxygen to the launch pad without laying pipes.
infinite_horizon.handbook.phase_2.strom_: On the Moon there is neither coal nor kerosene at your doorstep. The <item:infinite_horizon:solar_panel> makes power from sunlight, and <item:infinite_horizon:aluminum_cable> carries more power than copper.
Put a few solar panels and a battery next to every Moon base. During the day they charge the battery, at night it supplies dome and machines.

A solar panel needs **open sky** above it. Then it supplies 5 J/t during the day, multiplied by the **solar factor** of the location. At dusk the output drops, at night it is 0. In rain it only brings 25 %.
The panel pushes its power into all adjacent cables and machines. Its buffer covers short breaks; for the night you need a [[infinite_horizon:phase_1/strom|battery]].
No sunlight reaches the Moon's polar craters. A solar panel supplies nothing there.

An <item:infinite_horizon:aluminum_cable> carries 2,048 J/t, a <item:infinite_horizon:copper_cable> only 256 J/t. Cables of different kinds do not connect directly. For the transition, put a battery in between.
infinite_horizon.handbook.phase_2.weltra: On long journeys inventory space is scarce. The <item:infinite_horizon:food_packer> presses 3 food items of any kind into a <item:infinite_horizon:space_ration>. The ration fills you as much as all ingredients together, at most 20 hunger points and 20 saturation. Rations stack up to 16.
The research node "Space food" unlocks the food packer, see [[infinite_horizon:phase_2/forschung|Research]].
Set up the food packer and connect it to power.
Put one food item into each input slot. They may be different.
After one operation the ration lies in the output slot. The tooltip shows how much it fills.
Use filling ingredients like bread, baked potatoes or steak. They make a ration that almost completely satisfies your hunger.
infinite_horizon.handbook.phase_3.ereign: Alien worlds have their own weather. Every 1,200 t (60 s) the server rolls for every world with players whether an event comes. It starts 2,400 t (120 s) later, and 400 t (20 s) before that you get a warning in chat, a warning tone and a display in the HUD. The server sets how often events come with `event_frequency`.
With a running [[infinite_horizon:phase_4/wetterstation|space weather station]] of your agency in the same world, the warning comes 2,400 t (120 s) in advance.

On Venus it rains acid. Anyone standing unprotected under the open sky loses durability on armor and tools in hand every 40 t (2 s). The [[infinite_horizon:phase_3/hitzeanzug|heat suit]] protects you.
Do not leave valuable machines unprotected under the open sky on Mars and the Moon. A roof of three blocks protects them in a solar storm.
A meteor shower is a good opportunity: collect the impacts while it lasts.
On every world except Earth. Radiation rises by 2. Machines without a roof of at least 3 blocks stop every 200 t (10 s) for 40 t (2 s). In return, solar panels supply 2 times as much.

On the Moon and Mars. Every 100 t (5 s) a meteorite strikes within 64 blocks of every player. It explodes without fire (the server decides whether blocks are destroyed) and leaves <item:infinite_horizon:meteorite_ore>. In the [[infinite_horizon:phase_1/zerkleinerer|crusher]] that gives iron, nickel and with luck <item:infinite_horizon:raw_platinum> or <item:infinite_horizon:raw_iridium>.

Instead of rain, dust storms sweep over Mars. Solar panels only supply 0.25 times as much, monsters come twice as often, and dust wraiths appear that can lead you to exploration targets (see [[infinite_horizon:phase_3/kreaturen|Creatures]]).
infinite_horizon.handbook.phase_3.erste_: In the third phase you learn to survive on alien worlds. First with a suit and an oxygen supply, later under protective domes.
**Make oxygen.** The [[infinite_horizon:phase_3/sauerstoffgenerator|oxygen generator]] makes oxygen from power, the electrolyzer from water.
**Fill canisters.** Put [[infinite_horizon:phase_2/sauerstoff|oxygen canisters]] into the fill slot and take them out full.
**Put on the suit.** Wear all four pieces of the [[infinite_horizon:phase_2/raumanzug|pressure suit]]. The chestplate refills from the canisters in your inventory.
**Out into the vacuum.** Watch the HUD: the bars show strain and suit oxygen (see [[infinite_horizon:start/umwelt|Environment, Strain and Gravity]]).
**Build a dome.** A [[infinite_horizon:phase_3/kuppel|dome generator]] with power and oxygen creates breathable air for your base. You may also sleep there.
**Light without fire.** Outside nothing burns. Use <item:infinite_horizon:electric_lamp> instead of torches, see [[infinite_horizon:phase_3/leben_ohne_luft|Living Without Air]].
**Mark the landing site.** A [[infinite_horizon:phase_3/landefeuer|landing beacon]] at your Moon base is the target for all further flights of your agency.

**Grow food.** Under the dome, food grows on [[infinite_horizon:phase_3/hydrokultur|compost soil or in the hydroponics basin]]. For the road, the [[infinite_horizon:phase_2/weltraumnahrung|food packer]] packs rations.
Build an oxygen generator with a pressure bottle on the Moon early. Then you can refill your canisters on site.
infinite_horizon.handbook.phase_3.helium: The Moon's soil contains helium that the solar wind deposited there over billions of years. Heat gets it out, cold makes it liquid.
Put the regolith heater right into your Moon base and pipe the helium into a gas tank. You can then run the liquefier on Earth as well.

The <item:infinite_horizon:regolith_heater> heats <item:infinite_horizon:moon_regolith> and releases helium into its tank. It works **only on the Moon**. Anywhere else its lamp glows red, and the tooltip tells you why.
The <item:infinite_horizon:cryo_liquefier> cools helium so much that it turns liquid. The <item:infinite_horizon:cooling_system> of the heat suits needs liquid helium.
You store gases in the <item:infinite_horizon:gas_tank>. It only takes gases and outputs them through a selectable side, like the fluid tank.
infinite_horizon.handbook.phase_3.hitzea: The **heat suit** is the second suit tier. You build it from your [[infinite_horizon:phase_2/raumanzug|pressure suit]]: every piece is upgraded in the assembly table and keeps its oxygen and modules.
You install modules in the assembly table: put the suit piece and the module in together. Every piece has 2 module slots, and modules fit every suit tier.
The <item:infinite_horizon:cooling_system> in the chestplate needs liquid helium, see [[infinite_horizon:phase_3/helium|Helium and Cryogenics]].
**Pressure:** high pressure as on Venus as well.
**Oxygen:** from the chestplate as with the pressure suit, using 1 mB every 20 t (1 s).

On the surface of Venus, below the cloud layer (y 180), even the heat suit does not last forever. A separate bar in the HUD shows the **heat time**: 3,600 t (180 s). Once it has run out, the suit no longer protects you from heat.
Above the cloud layer the heat time refills in 1,200 t (60 s). So take the [[infinite_horizon:phase_3/venus|cloud elevator]] up in good time.
The heat time runs even if you only want to go down briefly. Check the bar before every descent.
infinite_horizon.handbook.phase_3.hochte: Tungsten only melts at temperatures the electric furnace cannot reach. For that you build the <item:infinite_horizon:high_temperature_furnace>. It also fires <item:infinite_horizon:ceramic_plate> for the heat suits.
Lightweight construction and electronics of the second research tier are made in the assembly table:
A <item:infinite_horizon:magnesium_ingot>, a <item:infinite_horizon:tungsten_ingot> and some helium from your machines open research tier 3. See [[infinite_horizon:phase_2/forschung|Research]].
infinite_horizon.handbook.phase_3.hydrok: On the Moon and Mars nothing grows in the soil. Regolith and Mars sand cannot be tilled. For food you have two ways: compost soil for classic fields or the hydroponics basin. The research node "Hydroponics" unlocks both.
Outside Earth, all plants need an active [[infinite_horizon:phase_3/kuppel|dome]] and enough light.
An electric lamp above the basin gives enough light, even in the lunar night.

Right-clicking a hydroponics basin or a greenhouse with <item:infinite_horizon:ammonia_fertilizer> fertilizes it for 24,000 t (1,200 s). During that time the plants grow faster. You make the fertilizer at the assembly table from bone meal and ammonia.

<item:infinite_horizon:compost_soil> is made in the assembly table from regolith or Mars sand, bone meal and gypsum or <item:infinite_horizon:compost>. A hoe turns it into <item:infinite_horizon:compost_farmland>. It behaves like farmland on Earth: it needs water nearby and otherwise dries back into compost soil.

The <item:infinite_horizon:hydroponics_basin> needs power, water and light (at least 9). Put seeds or a sapling into the planting slot. The plant grows one stage every 2,000 t (100 s), about twice as fast as on good farmland. Once ripe, the harvest lands in the output slot and the seed stays in the planting slot. A sapling needs 2 stages and gives 4 logs of its wood type.
If the dome fails or it gets too dark, the plant stops growing. The status lamp then shows "No growth".
infinite_horizon.handbook.phase_3.kreatu: More lives on the alien worlds than you would think. Most creatures are harmless, some are useful, one is dangerous. With the <item:infinite_horizon:field_scanner> you analyze them: right-clicking a creature gives your agency 15 RP the first time for each species.
Analyze each species once: that is easy research points on every new world.

**Rubble crawler:** lies camouflaged like a stone until you come closer than 3 blocks. It eats cables and metal blocks outside domes, one every 200 t (10 s). If you attack it, it fights back. It drops <item:infinite_horizon:metal_concentrate>, which gives metal in the crusher.
**Shade strider:** shy, flees from light and from you. Follow it long enough and it leads you to ice or ore nearby.

**Dune burrower:** digs invisibly through the sand and is drawn by vibrations, such as a running crusher or the drill of your [[infinite_horizon:phase_3/rover|rover]]. It attacks players and drops <item:infinite_horizon:armor_plate>.
**Dust wraith:** floats peacefully and is immune to arrows. If you get close, it usually leads you to a lava tube or a meteorite field and then vanishes.
**Sulfur snail:** fireproof, leaves a thin <item:infinite_horizon:sulfur_trail> that disappears after a while and now and then lays <item:infinite_horizon:sulfur>. Sulfur makes it breed.
**Cloud ray:** flies around peacefully. You can tame it with <item:infinite_horizon:sulfur> (not every attempt succeeds), and with a saddle it becomes a flying mount. It flies where you look.
Dune burrowers only come out in the dark. A running machine on Mars draws them from far away.
Creatures of the Inner Solar System
infinite_horizon.handbook.phase_3.kuppel: Under a dome you can breathe and work without a suit. The <item:infinite_horizon:dome_generator_t1> spreads an invisible hemisphere around itself. Inside there is breathable air, normal pressure and a pleasant 20 °C.
The **Dome I** node in tier 2 unlocks the dome generator ([[infinite_horizon:phase_2/forschung|Research]]).

The <item:infinite_horizon:dome_generator_t2> spreads a dome with radius 16 and withstands outside temperatures from -210 to 250 °C. Beneath it you are also protected from dust storms and acid rain (see [[infinite_horizon:phase_3/ereignisse|Space Weather]]): solar panels supply full power in a dust storm.

The <item:infinite_horizon:dome_generator_t3> spreads a dome with radius 32 and withstands -250 to 300 °C. It also shields against radiation and solar storms: machines beneath it do not pause in a solar storm.
Every dome generator has 3 module slots. Each module fits in once.
<item:infinite_horizon:dome_shield_module>: intercepts meteorites. It does not stop monsters.
Connect a pressure bottle or a second oxygen generator to the dome generator. Then the supply lasts even when you are away for a while.
Put the generator in the middle of your base. The dome reaches 8 blocks and starts one block below the generator.

Fill its **oxygen tank**: through pipes, an adjacent [[infinite_horizon:phase_3/sauerstoffgenerator|oxygen generator]] or [[infinite_horizon:phase_2/sauerstoff|canisters]] in the drain slot. The fact sheet above shows how much it uses.
With power and oxygen supplied and a suitable outside temperature, the dome runs at once. The lamp on the generator turns green, and points of light sparkle at the edge of the dome.
The generator measures the outside temperature where it stands. It must be between -180 and 150 °C, otherwise the dome does not start (red lamp). Overlapping domes form a shared air space.
If a player in a [[infinite_horizon:phase_2/raumanzug|pressure suit]] stands in the dome, the generator refills their oxygen from its tank as long as at least 500 mB are left there.

If power or oxygen run out or the temperature no longer fits, the dome goes into **failure**: the points of light pulse red, all players inside get a warning with the seconds left, and a warning tone sounds. The dome still protects for 600 t (30 s), then it is off. If the supply returns before that, it keeps running right away.
Once the dome is off, the planet's vacuum applies there again. Anyone standing inside without a suit builds up strain immediately. Always keep a filled suit within reach.
infinite_horizon.handbook.phase_3.landef: The <item:infinite_horizon:landing_beacon> marks a landing site. On the navigation map ([[infinite_horizon:phase_2/flug|The Flight]]) it appears as a landing site for all members of your agency.
Place the landing beacon where your rockets should land. It belongs to the agency of whoever places it.
**Right-click** opens a name field (up to 50 characters). Without its own name it takes the name of the item renamed at an anvil, or "Landing beacon X/Z".
Under the open sky, a red beam up to height 256 shows where it stands.
The navigation map knows all landing beacons of your agency, even on bodies where nobody is right now. If you break it, it disappears from the list.
If you choose a landing beacon as the landing site, the rocket lands at most 3 blocks away from it, but never on the beacon itself. If there is no room, it searches the wider area as usual.
Leave some space on flat, solid ground around the landing beacon. Then the rocket stands right next to it after landing.
infinite_horizon.handbook.phase_3.leben_: On every alien world, special rules apply outside an active [[infinite_horizon:phase_3/kuppel|dome]], no matter what the atmosphere is like. On Earth, in the Nether and in the End everything stays as usual.
Build your base so that bed and dome generator stand close together. A bed at the edge of the dome quickly ends up outside.
The **Dome I** node in tier 2 unlocks the electric lamp ([[infinite_horizon:phase_2/forschung|Research]]).
Inside the dome, torches and campfires work quite normally. Electric lamps are worth it mostly outside and in caves.
**Torches, fire, campfires, lanterns and candles** cannot be placed outside. Redstone torches keep working.
Existing torches go out one by one and turn into <item:infinite_horizon:extinguished_torch>. Campfires and candles go out, lanterns and fire disappear.
The <item:infinite_horizon:electric_lamp> brings light. It shines at full strength everywhere, but needs power: 5 J/t. Without power it stays dark.
**Plants** do not grow outside; bone meal does not help either.
**Water** freezes into ice at once on the Moon, and that ice does not melt there.
On alien worlds a bed sets your spawn point only **inside an active dome**. Outside, "You can't breathe here" appears and you cannot sleep.
If the dome fails while you are dead, your spawn point is no longer safe. You then appear at Earth's world spawn.
infinite_horizon.handbook.phase_3.mars.e: Mars is colder and farther away than the Moon, but it has a thin atmosphere and resources the Moon lacks: magnesium, nickel and gypsum.
A canyon saves you a lot of digging: the ores lie open on the walls.
**Air:** thin and not breathable. Without a [[infinite_horizon:phase_2/raumanzug|suit]] you will not survive long.
**Mars Red Plains:** wide red plains of <item:infinite_horizon:mars_sand>, with magnesium and iron in the ground.
**Mars Canyon:** deep gorges almost down to the bottom of the world. The ore layers lie exposed on the walls.
**Mars Volcanic Highlands:** high mountains of <item:infinite_horizon:mars_rock>. The giant volcanoes stand here, and lava tubes run deep in the rock.
**Mars Meteorite Field:** small craters with <item:infinite_horizon:iron_nickel_meteorite> in the middle. A whole meteorite field is an exploration target and brings research points.
5 veins per chunk, up to 8 blocks each
4 veins per chunk, up to 8 blocks each
10 veins per chunk, up to 8 blocks each
8 veins per chunk, up to 8 blocks each

From <item:infinite_horizon:iron_nickel_meteorite> you get <item:infinite_horizon:raw_nickel> and sometimes Raw Iron. You process magnesium and nickel like iron: into dust in the [[infinite_horizon:phase_1/zerkleinerer|crusher]], into ingots in the <item:infinite_horizon:electric_furnace>.
The nights on Mars are icy. Plan your trips so that you are back in the dome before dark.
infinite_horizon.handbook.phase_3.rakete: Mars and Venus are too far for the first [[infinite_horizon:phase_2/rakete|rocket]]. The T2 rocket runs on **hydrogen and oxygen**, has room for 2 people and needs a bigger launch pad.
Simply extend your 5×5 pad with a ring of pad blocks. The T1 rocket still launches from the centre.

The T2 rocket only launches from a platform of 7 × 7 pad blocks; everything else is as with the [[infinite_horizon:phase_2/raumfahrt|launch pad]]. The tower must be as tall as the rocket. A landed T2 rocket also launches without a pad.
<item:infinite_horizon:rocket_engine_t2> on the centre, 4 <item:infinite_horizon:rocket_fin_t2> next to it.
One tank holds 16,000 mB each of hydrogen and oxygen. The [[infinite_horizon:phase_1/elektrolyseur|electrolyzer]] supplies both, and the pump fills the tanks as with T1.

Research **Planetary probes** and send one [[infinite_horizon:phase_2/raumfahrt|probe]] each to Mars and Venus. Then both appear on the [[infinite_horizon:phase_2/flug|navigation map]]. See [[infinite_horizon:phase_3/mars|Mars]] and [[infinite_horizon:phase_3/venus|Venus]].
On foot the distances on Mars and the Moon are long. The rover carries you and one passenger across the terrain at 0.4 blocks per tick and climbs steps up to 2 blocks high.
Setting up and driving
Dismantling
Sneak and right-click with an empty hand: the rover becomes a kit again. Energy, oxygen, modules and cargo are kept inside.
On the surface of Venus the rover stops after 3,600 t (180 s) until it is back above y 180. The cloud elevator takes rovers nearby along.
Crafting
Put a battery in your base and park the rover there. That way it is full before every drive.
Right-clicking the ground with the <item:infinite_horizon:rover_kit> sets up the rover.
Right-click to get in. Whoever gets in first drives: the rover follows your view direction, and you drive forward and backward with the movement keys.
Sneaking lets you get out.
Energy
The rover stores 100,000 J and needs 50 J per block driven.
**Solar roof:** 2 J per tick under the open sky.
**Charging:** park the rover right next to a <item:infinite_horizon:battery>. It hands out 512 J per tick.
Cargo hold and modules
The cargo hold has 27 slots. You open it with the inventory key in the seat, or by sneaking and right-clicking (with an item in hand).
You insert up to 6 modules with a right-click:
<item:infinite_horizon:rover_scanner>: every 100 t (5 s) it counts the ores within 32 blocks and names exploration targets nearby.
<item:infinite_horizon:rover_drill>: while driving it mines the 3 × 3 blocks in front of the rover; the drops land in the cargo hold.
<item:infinite_horizon:rover_headlight>: a bright headlight in front of the rover.

<item:infinite_horizon:rover_pressure_cabin>: passengers breathe without a suit at a pleasant temperature as long as the tank (1,800 mB) has oxygen. Right-clicking with a filled [[infinite_horizon:phase_2/sauerstoff|oxygen canister]] fills it.
<item:infinite_horizon:rover_trailer>: 27 extra cargo slots.
The Rover
infinite_horizon.handbook.phase_3.sauers: The <item:infinite_horizon:oxygen_generator> makes oxygen from power alone. Unlike the electrolyzer it needs no water and therefore works everywhere, even on the dry Moon.
Set up the generator and supply it with power.
Every 1,200 t (60 s) it produces 100 mB of oxygen into its internal buffer.
Through its **output side** it hands the oxygen to tanks, pressure bottles or pipes. You choose the side with the "Side" button.
An empty [[infinite_horizon:phase_2/sauerstoff|oxygen canister]] in the **fill slot** is filled at once.
The **Dome I** node in tier 2 unlocks the oxygen generator ([[infinite_horizon:phase_2/forschung|Research]]).
It needs a <item:infinite_horizon:pressure_hull>. The pressure hull is a component for everything under pressure.
The electrolyzer supplies oxygen much more cheaply as long as you have water. On the Moon the generator is the simplest source.
Venus is the hottest place in the inner solar system. Beneath a dense, toxic cloud cover lie lava lakes and volcanoes, but also tungsten and sulfur.
4 veins per chunk, up to 8 blocks each
5 veins per chunk, up to 6 blocks each
<item:infinite_horizon:venus_tungsten_ore> needs an iron pickaxe. Sulfur ore gives several pieces of <item:infinite_horizon:sulfur> at once.
Build your base in the cloud layer and only go down to mine.
**Lava sea:** up to height 40 everything is filled with lava.

Between y 180 and 240 lies the cloud layer. It is pleasantly warm there and the pressure is normal; only the air stays toxic. All rockets land here: if there is no ground at the landing site yet, the server builds a platform of <item:infinite_horizon:aerostat_platform> at y 200.
**<item:infinite_horizon:aerostat_platform>:** a floating block. Place more next to it to enlarge your platform.

**<item:infinite_horizon:cloud_elevator>:** put it on the platform and right-click. After 100 t (5 s) you stand on the surface below, where the lower station is created automatically. If there is lava, a small platform of <item:infinite_horizon:venus_rock> is built. Right-clicking below takes you back up.
Down below, the [[infinite_horizon:phase_3/hitzeanzug|heat time]] of your suit runs. Without a heat suit you will not survive the surface.
**Venus Lava Plains:** basalt plains with lava lakes and sulfur.
**Venus Volcanoes:** volcanic cones of <item:infinite_horizon:venus_rock> and magma blocks, with tungsten in the rock. Volcanic vents lie on their flanks; they are exploration targets.
infinite_horizon.handbook.phase_4.erste_: In the fourth phase you leave the surfaces behind and build a space station. It is the hub for all further flights: a launch from the station costs no fuel for the ascent.
**Open tier 3.** Obtain helium, magnesium and tungsten, see [[infinite_horizon:phase_2/forschung|Research]].
**Fly into orbit.** A T2 rocket reaches Earth orbit. It is always known on the navigation map, see [[infinite_horizon:phase_4/orbit|The Orbit]].

**Place the station core.** Take a <item:infinite_horizon:station_core> along. A right-click from the capsule places it right below the rocket, see [[infinite_horizon:phase_4/raumstation|The Space Station]].
**Get out safely.** The core's built-in dome supplies you with air. With <item:infinite_horizon:magnet_boots> in your boots you walk on the station as on Earth.
**Expand the station.** Docking bay, tank depot, solar wing and habitat module turn the station into a hub, see [[infinite_horizon:phase_4/stationsmodule|Station Modules]].
**Commute.** With the [[infinite_horizon:phase_4/landefaehre|lander]] you fly between station and Earth or Moon without a big rocket.
**Power for the station.** A [[infinite_horizon:phase_4/fusionsreaktor|fusion reactor]] supplies power for the dome, fabricators and gravity plates.
Take a filled suit and oxygen canisters along. Until the core's dome is up, you are in a vacuum.
infinite_horizon.handbook.phase_4.fertig: Some materials can only be made in zero gravity. That is why the <item:infinite_horizon:zero_g_fabricator> only works in orbit; on a planet it shows an error. It needs power and, for many recipes, liquid helium from the [[infinite_horizon:phase_3/helium|cryo liquefier]].
<item:infinite_horizon:superconductor_wire> is the base material for superconductor cables and the fusion reactor.
As soon as a zero-g fabricator of your agency finishes its first operation, research tier 4 opens, see [[infinite_horizon:phase_2/forschung|Research]].
Without a dome, orbit is a vacuum. Put the fabricator under the station core's dome so you can work on it without a suit.
A tank depot with liquid helium next to the fabricator saves many flights to the Moon.
infinite_horizon.handbook.phase_4.fusion: The fusion reactor is the station's power plant: 1,000 J/t from hydrogen and helium. It is a large multiblock and constantly needs cooling with liquid helium.
A fusion reactor supplies more power than aluminium cables can carry. The <item:infinite_horizon:superconductor_cable> carries 32,768 J/t.
The <item:infinite_horizon:gravity_plate> needs a lot of power. In return, normal gravity applies above it in orbit: in an area of 9 × 9 blocks and 8 blocks high.
Put a cryo liquefier next to the output port: it turns the evaporated helium back into coolant.
The reactor is a cube of 5 × 5 × 5 blocks with a hollow interior.
Place the controller (<item:infinite_horizon:fusion_reactor>). Its front faces you.
The controller is the **middle of one side face**: the cube extends two blocks left, right, up and down from it and four blocks back.
Build the shell from <item:infinite_horizon:fusion_casing>. The interior of 3 × 3 × 3 blocks stays air.
Replace single casing blocks with **ports** where pipes and cables should connect, as with the [[infinite_horizon:phase_1/raffinerie|refinery]].
As soon as everything is right, the status lamp turns from red to yellow.
**Sneak-right-click** the controller with an empty hand to see red particles where blocks are still missing.

Every 20 t (1 s) the reactor burns 10 mB of hydrogen and 5 mB of helium. For cooling it needs 2 mB of liquid helium from the [[infinite_horizon:phase_3/helium|cryo liquefier]] at the same rate. The evaporated helium ends up in the output tank and can go back into the cycle.
If cooling is missing for 40 t (2 s), the reactor shuts down and the lamp turns red. It does not explode. It restarts by itself once cooling has run for 100 t (5 s) without interruption.
infinite_horizon.handbook.phase_4.landef: A rocket is built for long distances. For the short way between your station and the ground below there is the <item:infinite_horizon:lander>. It has 2 seats and a tank with 32,000 mB of hydrogen and as much oxygen.
Right-clicking a block in orbit or a [[infinite_horizon:phase_4/stationsmodule|docking bay]] with the lander sets it down, like a boat. That does not work on a planet.
Fuel it like a rocket: through the slot pair in the window, or on a docking bay with tanks next to it.
Sit down, open the window with the inventory key and press "Launch".

The lander only commutes between an orbit and the bodies below: from Earth orbit to Earth and the Moon, from Mars orbit to Mars, from Venus orbit to Venus. The navigation map only shows these destinations. A flight costs the launch and the landing, but no transfer, see [[infinite_horizon:phase_2/rakete|Fuel]].
The lander does not launch from Earth's surface. Bring it into orbit with a rocket and leave it there.
A lander on a docking bay with a tank depot next to it is quickly full again after every return.
Above Earth, Mars and Venus lies an orbit each. There is no ground there, only emptiness, the Sun and the planet far below you. Gravity is only 0.005 g: walking on blocks works normally, but whoever jumps drifts away.

A T2 rocket flies into orbit. Without a docking bay it hovers at height 100 at the chosen spot. If something is already in the way there, or a foreign station core is closer than 64 blocks, the on-board computer looks for a free spot nearby. A launch from orbit costs no fuel for the ascent.
<item:infinite_horizon:magnet_boots> are a suit module for the boots. If a block is directly below you, 1 g applies. Jump off and you float again.

If you fall below height 0, you plunge onto the planet below: onto Earth, Mars or into the cloud layer of Venus, at the same spot. A slow fall of 400 t (20 s) catches you. The rocket and your station stay up there.
First build a railing of hull blocks around the platform. Then you do not drift off so easily when jumping.
infinite_horizon.handbook.phase_4.raumst: Every station starts with a <item:infinite_horizon:station_core>. It can only be placed in orbit, even in mid-air: without a target block it lands 3 blocks in front of you, and from a rocket's capsule right below it. Everything within 48 blocks belongs to the station.
Placing it creates a platform of 5 × 5 blocks of <item:infinite_horizon:station_hull>. These platform blocks drop nothing when mined.
A built-in dome with radius 8 creates breathable air. It needs oxygen in the tank (2,000 mB) and power.
The power comes from 4 built-in solar cells with 20 J/t each times the orbit's solar factor. The core also accepts power through cables.
<item:infinite_horizon:station_hull> is the building block for walls and floors, <item:infinite_horizon:station_window> is transparent like glass.
Without oxygen in the tank, the core's dome goes out like any other dome. Keep the tank filled through pipes or pressure bottles.
You fill the oxygen tank like the dome generator's, through the fill slot or an adjacent oxygen generator.
infinite_horizon.handbook.phase_4.statio: Around the [[infinite_horizon:phase_4/raumstation|station core]] you expand your station with modules. All modules only work in orbit, except the tank depot, which works everywhere.
An analyzer directly next to the <item:infinite_horizon:research_lab> brings 1.5 times as many research points.

The <item:infinite_horizon:greenhouse> works like 9 [[infinite_horizon:phase_3/hydrokultur|hydroponics basins]] at once. It needs power, water, light, an active dome and one <item:infinite_horizon:dry_ice> in the last input slot every 6,000 t (300 s).
The habitat module only sets the respawn point inside an active dome. If it fails, you reappear on Earth after death.
Put a tank depot with hydrogen and oxygen right next to the docking bay. Then your rocket is quickly full again after every landing.

The <item:infinite_horizon:docking_bay> is a landing pad for rockets. Like a landing beacon it appears in your agency's choice of landing sites and can be named with a right-click. If you choose it as the destination, the rocket touches down right on it. A rocket standing on the bay refuels from adjacent tanks, as fast as at a fuel pump.
The <item:infinite_horizon:tank_depot> holds 256,000 mB of one fluid. It outputs only through its output side; all other sides accept. Next to the docking bay it is your station's fuel store.
The <item:infinite_horizon:solar_wing> supplies 20 J/t times the solar factor in orbit, as long as it sees the Sun. On a planet it supplies nothing.

The <item:infinite_horizon:habitation_module> is bed and storage in one: right-clicking sets your respawn point above the module and opens 27 storage slots. The respawn point only applies under an active dome.
infinite_horizon.handbook.phase_4.wetter: The <item:infinite_horizon:space_weather_station> watches the Sun and the sky. As long as it has power, it warns all members of your agency in the same world 2,400 t (120 s) before an event instead of only 400 t (20 s) before. It works everywhere except on Earth and needs an owner.
One station per world is enough: the early warning covers the whole dimension. See [[infinite_horizon:phase_3/ereignisse|Space Weather and Events]].
infinite_horizon.handbook.phase_5.astero: In the asteroid belt there is no ground, only boulders in empty space. Gravity is 0.03 g: a jump carries you far, and whoever misses drifts away.
The <item:infinite_horizon:asteroid_anchor> is placed on an asteroid. Within 16 blocks, 1 g then applies to players: that is how you build a base without floating away.
Swarms of drift mites float around asteroids with platinum ore. They are harmless and show you where platinum is. They only spawn with the world and do not come back.
Follow a drift mite swarm: it gives away the asteroid with platinum before you even mine it.
The small asteroids have a radius of 3 to 12 blocks, and there are big ones with 13 to 20 blocks. They consist of <item:infinite_horizon:asteroid_rock> with ores inside:
At spawn at X/Z 0/0 there is always a big asteroid with all three ores.
If you fall below height 0, navigation brings you back to the spawn asteroid with slow falling. Whatever you drop on the way is lost.

You process platinum and iridium like other ores: crusher and electric furnace. The <item:infinite_horizon:iridium_chip> is made in the [[infinite_horizon:phase_4/fertigung_im_orbit|zero-g fabricator]] and goes into many devices of the fifth phase.
Ceres is the largest body in the asteroid belt: a dwarf planet with 0.03 g, cold (-110 to -90 °C) and without air. A pressure suit is enough.
Near the landing site at X/Z 0/0 stands a cone of ice, the only ice volcano on Ceres. Whoever sets foot on it earns their agency research points as an exploration target.
On Ceres nothing grows without a dome, and water freezes at once. Take oxygen for the whole trip.
The volcano's ice is a convenient water supply for a base on Ceres.
infinite_horizon.handbook.phase_5.eisrie: Uranus and Neptune are the ice giants at the edge of the planetary system. As with Jupiter and Saturn you only reach their orbits, and only with the [[infinite_horizon:phase_5/fernflug|long-range module]]. From Neptune orbit the [[infinite_horizon:phase_4/landefaehre|lander]] flies to the moon [[infinite_horizon:phase_5/triton|Triton]].
The gas collector at the ice giants
A [[infinite_horizon:phase_5/jupiter|gas collector]] in Uranus or Neptune orbit collects 100 mB of methane every 20 ticks. With the **Mode** button in the GUI you switch to hydrogen and back.
Empty the tank before you switch. As long as the other gas is still inside, the collector cannot add anything.
Whoever falls below the station does not land on the planet, but on the nearest station core, and takes damage.
infinite_horizon.handbook.phase_5.encela: Enceladus is a small, icy moon of Saturn without air. At -200 °C it is so cold that you need a [[infinite_horizon:phase_3/hitzeanzug|tier 2 suit]]. At 0.01 g, gravity is almost zero.
**Tiger stripes** of <item:infinite_horizon:enceladus_ice>, with one ammonia geyser per chunk.

Every 200 t (10 s) an <item:infinite_horizon:ammonia_geyser> erupts and shoots a fountain 40 blocks high. Whoever stands in the fountain is hurled upwards at 2 blocks per tick. Geysers cannot be mined.
In the low gravity you float for a long time after a geyser jump. That is a quick way onto high ice ridges.
Do not build directly above a geyser. The fountain lifts everything standing above it.
The **geyser moth** circles around the geysers. It is harmless; where you see it, a geyser is not far.
infinite_horizon.handbook.phase_5.erste_: Research tier 4 opens the solar system beyond the Moon, Mars and Venus. Every destination there demands its own equipment: heat, cold and radiation are harsher than in ring 1.

**Build the advanced probe.** The "Advanced probe" node unlocks the <item:infinite_horizon:advanced_probe> and all destinations in ring 2. It launches from the [[infinite_horizon:phase_2/raumfahrt|launch pad]] like the simple probe and also reaches the old destinations.
**To Mercury.** [[infinite_horizon:phase_5/merkur|Mercury]] has lithium. Take a heat suit and a radiation shield.
**Process lithium.** Lithium salt becomes ingots, and those become [[infinite_horizon:phase_5/lithium|lithium batteries]], the basis of all devices of the fourth phase.

**Into the asteroid belt.** The [[infinite_horizon:phase_5/asteroiden|asteroids]] hold platinum and iridium, which make iridium chips. On [[infinite_horizon:phase_5/ceres|Ceres]] an ice volcano waits as an exploration target.
**To Jupiter.** In [[infinite_horizon:phase_5/jupiter|Jupiter orbit]] the gas collector gathers hydrogen. The lander takes you on to the volcanic moon [[infinite_horizon:phase_5/io|Io]].

**Under Europa's ice.** With ice drill and dive module you reach the ocean of [[infinite_horizon:phase_5/europa|Europa]]. You need the microbial cultures from the vents for the [[infinite_horizon:phase_5/klonkammer|clone chamber]].

**To Saturn.** With the long-range module you reach [[infinite_horizon:phase_5/saturn|Saturn orbit]] and open tier 5. The lander takes you to [[infinite_horizon:phase_5/titan|Titan]] and [[infinite_horizon:phase_5/enceladus|Enceladus]].
**Antimatter.** The [[infinite_horizon:phase_5/magnetfalle|magnetic trap]] in Jupiter orbit fills antimatter cells.

**To the ice giants.** In [[infinite_horizon:phase_5/eisriesen|Uranus and Neptune orbit]] you collect methane. For [[infinite_horizon:phase_5/triton|Triton]] you need the [[infinite_horizon:phase_5/tiefraumanzug|deep space suit]] with a heating module.

**Pluto and the transmitter.** [[infinite_horizon:phase_5/pluto|Pluto]] has uranium. Beneath the heart glacier the [[infinite_horizon:phase_5/sender|transmitter]] waits with its sentinel, guarding the star chart.
The advanced probe costs more than the simple one. Send it first to the destination whose resources you need next.
First Steps in the Outer System
infinite_horizon.handbook.phase_5.europa: Europa is wrapped in a thick ice shell. Beneath it lies an ocean with warm vents bubbling on its floor. Gravity is 0.13 g, the surface is -160 °C cold, and Jupiter's radiation is at level 2.
Only drill where you can get out again. A staircase of blocks or a jetpack brings you back up onto the ice shell.

On the sea floor lie **vent fields**: groups of <item:infinite_horizon:hydrothermal_vent> with bubbles rising from them. A vent field is an exploration target. Right-clicking a vent with an empty glass bottle gives a <item:infinite_horizon:microbe_culture>. Afterwards that vent rests for 1,200 t (60 s).
The **ice jelly** glows and drifts slowly towards the nearest vent. Follow it when you are looking for a vent field.
A **reef keeper** guards every vent field. It is peaceful until someone near it (radius 16 blocks) mines blocks or takes samples. Then it attacks (12 damage).
Give the reef keeper a space ration (right-click). It then stays peaceful towards you for 12,000 t (600 s), and you can take samples in peace.
**Ice shell** of <item:infinite_horizon:europa_ice> between y 112 and 124. It splits open in the **ice rifts**; there you reach the water directly.
**Ocean** below. Under the ice shell the water is 2 °C warm, the pressure normal and the radiation shielded.
At the surface: a space suit with a <item:infinite_horizon:radiation_shield>.
In the ocean from y 79 downwards there is deep-sea pressure. For that you need the <item:infinite_horizon:diving_module> on the leggings. It also makes you swim faster (×1.5).
Without a dive module the deep-sea pressure crushes you. Stay above the limit until you have one.

Europa ice is as hard as obsidian. With a pickaxe a shaft through the ice shell takes a very long time. The <item:infinite_horizon:ice_drill> is faster: hold the right mouse button, and it drills a shaft of 3 × 3 blocks downwards below you, one layer every 10 t (0.5 s). Each block costs 20 J from the battery (full: 100,000 J). Charge it in the charging slot of a battery.
infinite_horizon.handbook.phase_5.fernfl: A T2 rocket only reaches the outer destinations beyond the asteroid belt with more fuel. That is what the long-range module is for, and the station in orbit becomes the launch pad.
While it pushes, it uses 40 J per tick.
When the energy is empty you fall again, slowly in orbit, with full gravity on a planet.

The <item:infinite_horizon:long_range_module> is a tier 2 rocket part. It sits between the tanks and the capsule and holds an extra 128,000 mB per fuel component. The distant destinations from Saturn on only become selectable with it.

You can build a T2 rocket directly on a [[infinite_horizon:phase_4/stationsmodule|docking bay]]: engine on the bay, fins around it, tanks, long-range module and capsule above, a control panel nearby. You need neither tower nor fuel pump there. The bay fills the tanks from tanks adjacent to it. T1 rockets do not launch from the bay.
A launch from the station costs no fuel for the ascent. So build the big rockets in orbit.
The <item:infinite_horizon:jetpack> is a module for the chestplate. It stores 200,000 J; charge it in the charging slot of a battery, also while installed in the chestplate.
Hold **jump**: gravity is cancelled and you rise at up to 0.4 blocks per tick.
**Forward**: 0.1 blocks per tick in your view direction.
infinite_horizon.handbook.phase_5.io.e0: Io is Jupiter's innermost large moon and full of volcanoes. The surface of <item:infinite_horizon:io_crust> is cold (-140 °C), but there is lava everywhere. Gravity is 0.18 g, and Jupiter's radiation is at level 3.
infinite_horizon.handbook.phase_5.io.e10: The chunks hit hard. Leave the vent's radius as soon as the warning comes.
infinite_horizon.handbook.phase_5.io.e11: After the eruption, fresh sulfur ore lies around in the open. Collect it before you move on.
Everywhere: a space suit with a <item:infinite_horizon:radiation_shield>.
Near lava the temperature rises to 300 °C. There you need a [[infinite_horizon:phase_3/hitzeanzug|heat suit]] with a radiation shield.
**Sulfur plains**, **lava lakes** and **volcanic fields**. Volcanic vents stand in the volcanic fields; whoever sets foot on one earns their agency research points as an exploration target.
<item:infinite_horizon:io_sulfur_ore> is everywhere in the crust and gives sulfur.
infinite_horizon.handbook.phase_5.io.e6: The sulfur salamander lives in the lava lakes and at the volcanic vents. It is fireproof and shoots sulfur globs at you from afar (5 damage per hit). When defeated it sometimes drops a <item:infinite_horizon:heat_scale>.
infinite_horizon.handbook.phase_5.io.e9: If a volcanic vent is near a player, it can erupt. You are warned in advance. During the eruption, chunks of sulfur ore rain down within 32 blocks of the vent. Distance is the only protection.
infinite_horizon.handbook.phase_5.jupite: Jupiter has no surface you can land on. A rocket only takes you into **Jupiter orbit**, an empty world above the gas giant. From there you fly with the [[infinite_horizon:phase_4/landefaehre|lander]] to the moons [[infinite_horizon:phase_5/io|Io]] and Europa.

Radiation in Jupiter orbit is at level 3. Every space suit needs a <item:infinite_horizon:radiation_shield> there. Whoever falls below the station does not land on the planet: they are brought back to the nearest [[infinite_horizon:phase_4/raumstation|station core]] and take 4 damage. If there is no core yet, a small platform of station hull is created.
Without a radiation shield, Jupiter orbit is deadly, even in a heat or pressure suit.

The <item:infinite_horizon:gas_collector> only works in the orbits of the gas giants. It needs no ingredients: every 20 ticks it puts 100 mB of gas into its tank, hydrogen in Jupiter orbit. Empty containers in the fill slot get filled, pipes draw the gas off.
A gas collector next to the station's tank depot supplies rockets and the fusion reactor with hydrogen without you having to bring water to the station.
infinite_horizon.handbook.phase_5.klonka: Far out, the way back from world spawn is very long. The <item:infinite_horizon:clone_chamber> brings you back to a place of your choice after death, even in another dimension.
Put the clone chamber in a safe place, for example under a dome or in a station.
Connect it to power. It needs power all the time, even when nobody is dying.
Put <item:infinite_horizon:microbe_culture> into the input slot. Microbial cultures come from the hydrothermal vents of [[infinite_horizon:phase_5/europa|Europa]].
Right-clicking the chamber binds you to it. Every player has exactly one chamber; a new binding replaces the old one.
If you die, you wake up above the chamber if it has power and contains at least one culture. It uses up one culture doing so. The chamber does not need to be loaded for this.
If the spot above the chamber is no longer safe without a suit, for example because the dome has failed, you appear at your bed or at world spawn.
A stack of cultures lasts for many trips. Top up the chamber before you fly to the outer moons.
infinite_horizon.handbook.phase_5.lithiu: Lithium comes as a salt crust from [[infinite_horizon:phase_5/merkur|Mercury]]. The crusher turns it into dust, the electric furnace into ingots. From the ingots you build the <item:infinite_horizon:lithium_battery>, a component of almost all devices of the fourth phase.
The <item:infinite_horizon:lithium_battery_bank> stores 4,000,000 J and outputs up to 4,096 J/t, through its output side like the battery.
The <item:infinite_horizon:rover_lithium_pack> is a module for the [[infinite_horizon:phase_3/rover|rover]]: with it, the rover holds 2 times as much energy.
Lithium salt gives the same amount of lithium in the crusher and the electric furnace. Skip the crusher as long as you need it for ores.
infinite_horizon.handbook.phase_5.magnet: In Jupiter's strong magnetic field, antiparticles can be trapped. That is why the <item:infinite_horizon:magnetic_trap> only works in [[infinite_horizon:phase_5/jupiter|Jupiter orbit]].
Build the magnetic trap in your station in Jupiter orbit and connect it to plenty of power.
Put an empty <item:infinite_horizon:antimatter_cell> into the input slot.
After a long operation the filled cell lies in the output slot. Filled cells shimmer.
The first filled cell is a step towards the last research tier. Start early, the operation takes a long time.
Without power the progress stops. Provide a battery or a fusion reactor in the station.
infinite_horizon.handbook.phase_5.merkur: Mercury turns so slowly that one side always glows and the other always freezes. Where you land depends on the X coordinate:
**Twilight belt** in between: a pleasant 20 °C. Here <item:infinite_horizon:mercury_lithium_salt> lies as a crust at the surface.
**Shadow craters**: rare, -150 °C, with ice in the rock.
Do not look straight at the mirror beetle; approach it from the side. One hit from close range is usually enough.
4 veins per chunk, up to 6 blocks each
6 veins per chunk, up to 8 blocks each
4 veins per chunk, up to 16 blocks each

On the day side only the [[infinite_horizon:phase_3/hitzeanzug|heat suit]] helps. The suit alone does not protect against the radiation: install the <item:infinite_horizon:radiation_shield> in the helmet; it keeps out radiation up to level 3. The <item:infinite_horizon:heat_reflector> in the chestplate extends the heat time on Venus by 1.5 times.

The mirror beetle crawls around the twilight belt. It only attacks if you attack it. Its shell reflects the sunlight: whoever looks at it in daylight from less than 16 blocks is blinded for 60 t (3 s). It drops a <item:infinite_horizon:mirror_shell>, which makes the heat reflector.
Do not land on the day side without a heat suit. The twilight belt around X 0 is the safe landing site.
Pluto is the most distant destination in the solar system. The rocket needs the [[infinite_horizon:phase_5/fernflug|long-range module]] and lands directly on the surface. It is -230 °C cold, and gravity is 0.06 g.
A [[infinite_horizon:phase_3/hitzeanzug|tier 2 suit]] with a [[infinite_horizon:phase_5/tiefraumanzug|heating module]] is enough; the deep space suit is better.
Without a heating module you freeze to death on Pluto in any suit below tier 3.
**Heart glacier**: a wide plain of <item:infinite_horizon:pluto_nitrogen_ice> within 400 blocks of the landing site at X/Z 0/0. The [[infinite_horizon:phase_5/sender|transmitter]] lies beneath it.

Only the dark highlands hold <item:infinite_horizon:pluto_uranium_ore>, between y 0 and 60. You need an iron pickaxe. The crusher turns <item:infinite_horizon:raw_uranium> into <item:infinite_horizon:uranium_dust>, and only the electric furnace smelts that into <item:infinite_horizon:uranium_ingot>.
The first uranium ingot is a step towards the last research tier. Bring enough raw uranium for a whole furnace load.
infinite_horizon.handbook.phase_5.saturn: Saturn lies so far out that a T2 rocket only gets there with the [[infinite_horizon:phase_5/fernflug|long-range module]]. As with Jupiter you arrive in **Saturn orbit** above the gas giant. From there the [[infinite_horizon:phase_4/landefaehre|lander]] takes you to the moons [[infinite_horizon:phase_5/titan|Titan]] and [[infinite_horizon:phase_5/enceladus|Enceladus]].
As soon as a member of your agency sets foot in Saturn orbit, research tier 5 opens: the outer system.
A [[infinite_horizon:phase_5/jupiter|gas collector]] in Saturn orbit collects 100 mB of helium every 20 ticks.

Saturn's rings scatter debris. In a debris shower, chunks strike within 64 blocks of every player every 100 t (5 s), like a meteor shower but without ore. Only a dome's <item:infinite_horizon:dome_shield_module> intercepts them.
Without a shield module a debris shower hits your station too.
Do not fall below the station in Saturn orbit: as with Jupiter, the nearest station core brings you back, and that hurts.
infinite_horizon.handbook.phase_5.sender: Beneath the heart glacier on [[infinite_horizon:phase_5/pluto|Pluto]] lies a hall of <item:infinite_horizon:ancient_alloy> that nobody you know has built. The alloy cannot be mined. The <item:infinite_horizon:transmitter_core> stands in the middle.
Keep the star chart in a chest at your base. With it you will later go beyond the solar system.

Near the landing site a ring of ancient alloy marks the entrance. From there a stair tunnel of ice leads down to an opening in the south wall of the hall. Whoever enters the hall earns their agency research points as an exploration target.
Right-clicking the transmitter core wakes the **signal sentinel**, a boss with 400 health points:
As long as it has more than 50 % of its health, it strikes (10 damage) and every 100 t (5 s) it knocks everything within 6 blocks away with a shockwave.
Below that, it summons 3 frost lurkers and hits you with a beam if you stay in its gaze too long.
Every agency has its own sentinel. After a victory, the transmitter stays silent for your agency for 24,000 t (1,200 s).
The sentinel is the strongest enemy in the solar system. Come with full armor, healing potions and reinforcements.

When defeated, the sentinel drops your agency's <item:infinite_horizon:star_chart>. Every agency owns at most one. The chart does not burn and does not despawn when it lies around. If it is destroyed anyway, for example in the void, you can win a new one at the next victory.
infinite_horizon.handbook.phase_5.tiefra: The deep space suit is the tier 3 space suit. Like the [[infinite_horizon:phase_3/hitzeanzug|heat suit]] it protects against acid and heat, withstands -220 to 500 °C and shields radiation up to level 2. As armor it is as strong as netherite.

The <item:infinite_horizon:heating_module> goes into the chestplate and shifts the lower temperature limit by -30 °C. You need it with the deep space suit on [[infinite_horizon:phase_5/triton|Triton]], and with the heat suit on Pluto as well.
For the deep space suit you need insulation fabric from frost lurkers. Hunt them on Triton with a heat suit and heating module.
Titan is the only moon with a dense atmosphere. You cannot breathe it, but the pressure is normal, and it is -180 °C cold. Gravity is 0.14 g. A pressure suit is enough.
Whoever falls into a methane lake sinks as in water. Stay near the shore and take enough oxygen.
**Methane lakes**: up to y 62 the basins are filled with liquid Methane.
Instead of rain, **methane rain** falls on Titan.
In the dense air you sink more slowly with elytra (sink rate ×0.5). From an ice mountain that gets you far across the lakes.
Jump off a high peak with elytra. On Titan you glide farther than on Earth without fireworks.
The **methane skimmer** runs across the methane lakes. It flees as soon as you come closer than 12 blocks. When hunted it gives a <item:infinite_horizon:skimmer_leg>.
infinite_horizon.handbook.phase_5.triton: Triton is the coldest place you can reach: -235 °C. You cannot breathe its thin air. Gravity is 0.08 g.
No suit alone is enough here. You need the [[infinite_horizon:phase_5/tiefraumanzug|deep space suit]] with a heating module.
Without a heating module you freeze to death on Triton even in the deep space suit.
**Polar cap** and **geyser fields**, both rare. <item:infinite_horizon:nitrogen_geyser> stand in the geyser fields. They cannot be mined.

The **frost lurker** lies in wait in the ice. It is invisible until you come closer than 4 blocks; then it bursts out and attacks (7 damage). When defeated it sometimes drops <item:infinite_horizon:insulation_fabric>, the material for the deep space suit.
Walk slowly across the ice in the dark. If a frost lurker bursts out, you have a moment before it reaches you.
infinite_horizon.handbook.phase_6.aussen: An outpost is a <item:infinite_horizon:cargo_terminal> with all producers within 16 blocks. Producers are the [[infinite_horizon:phase_6/bohrturm|drilling rig and pump station]], the gas collector and the magnetic trap. They hand their yield straight to the terminal; you do not need to connect anything.

The terminal has 216 storage slots. Use the mouse wheel or the bar next to the storage to scroll through all rows. The tanks are on the right: the fuel tank on the far left, the cargo tanks next to it.
The fuel tank only takes methane. Incoming methane always fills it first; only the rest goes into the cargo tanks.
Clicking a tank bar selects the tank from which the fill slot fills empty containers.
Hoppers and pipes may put items in and take them out. Through its output side the terminal only hands out cargo, never the fuel.
If a producer belongs to two terminals, it always delivers to the nearer one.
The "Partners" button in the terminal releases it for your [[infinite_horizon:reference/agentur|partners]]. Their cargo rockets may then deliver here. They cannot take anything away.
If the outpost is not loaded because you are on another planet, the game calculates the extraction as soon as you come back. You then get 0.5 times the normal amount for the time that passed.

Only a producer that was running when you left counts. Power is not calculated, so make sure the supply is safe beforehand, for example with the [[infinite_horizon:phase_6/kernreaktor|fission reactor]].
Extraction stops when the terminal is full or inputs are missing, such as empty antimatter cells in the magnetic trap.
On servers, offline production can be switched off (setting `outposts_offline`).
infinite_horizon.handbook.phase_6.bohrtu: The drilling rig and the pump station are the producers of your outposts. They extract endlessly without changing the world.
You cannot set up the pump station directly on a lake. First place a <item:infinite_horizon:pontoon> on the fluid, like a lily pad. A pump station on the pontoon extracts from the fluid below.

In the [[infinite_horizon:phase_3/helium|cryo liquefier]] nitrogen becomes Liquid Nitrogen. It cools the [[infinite_horizon:phase_6/kernreaktor|fission reactor]] with a much smaller amount than water.

When set up, the <item:infinite_horizon:drilling_rig> counts all ore blocks in the chunk below it, down to the bottom of the world. After that it produces one ore every 100 t (5 s), weighted randomly by those counts: if there is much iron and little titanium below it, mostly iron comes out. The deposit never runs out.
The drilling rig does not work on Earth. If it finds no ores below it, its lamp glows red.
Put the drilling rig over an area with the ores you need, for example in the dark highlands on Pluto for uranium.
The <item:infinite_horizon:pump_station> extracts from the block directly below it, 100 mB every 20 t (1 s). The source stays.
Source block of water, lava, crude oil or methane
In the methane rain on Titan it extracts 1.5 times as much.
infinite_horizon.handbook.phase_6.erste_: In the last phase you connect your worlds. Outposts extract resources on their own, cargo rockets bring them to the shipyard in Earth orbit, and there the starship takes shape section by section.

**Build the fission reactor.** Uranium from [[infinite_horizon:phase_5/pluto|Pluto]] makes fuel rods. The [[infinite_horizon:phase_6/kernreaktor|fission reactor]] supplies more power than any other source.
**Extract.** [[infinite_horizon:phase_6/bohrturm|Drilling rig and pump station]] get ores and fluids without you mining yourself. On the geysers of Enceladus and Triton you gain ammonia and nitrogen.
**Found outposts.** A [[infinite_horizon:phase_6/aussenposten|cargo terminal]] collects everything the producers near it extract. Even while you are away, extraction keeps running.
**Fly cargo.** [[infinite_horizon:phase_6/frachtraketen|Cargo rockets]] in a terminal's hangar bring items and fluids to other terminals. Drives shorten the flight time.
**Set up routes.** At the [[infinite_horizon:phase_6/logistik_computer|logistics computer]] you decide when which rocket flies what where.
**Supply the shipyard.** In the [[infinite_horizon:phase_6/werft|orbital shipyard]] in Earth orbit your starship takes shape in eight sections.
**Launch.** After the eighth section you launch the [[infinite_horizon:phase_6/sternenschiff|starship]] at the shipyard terminal.
infinite_horizon.handbook.phase_6.fracht: Cargo rockets bring items and fluids from one [[infinite_horizon:phase_6/aussenposten|cargo terminal]] to another. You decide when they fly at the [[infinite_horizon:phase_6/logistik_computer|logistics computer]]. They do not fly visibly through the world: the game only remembers start, destination and arrival time. At launch and landing you see a small puff of smoke at the terminal.

To retrofit, put the rocket and the drive into the [[infinite_horizon:phase_1/montagetisch|assembly table]] together. Fuel and drive stay stored in the rocket. Only the best drive counts; a weaker one does not replace a better one.
For the antimatter drive you need charged antimatter cells from the magnetic trap. The assembly table does not accept empty cells.

Every cargo terminal has 4 hangar slots below the tanks. A rocket in a hangar slot belongs to that terminal; its flights always start there. While it is on its way, the item stays in the slot, is highlighted red and cannot be taken out.
The <item:infinite_horizon:cargo_rocket> has 4 holds of 27 slots each and 4 fluid holds. It flies on methane from its own tank (64,000 mB).
Before every launch it refuels from its terminal's fuel tank.
One leg costs 2,000 mB plus 1,500 mB per distance point between start and destination.
At the destination it unloads and refuels for the return flight from the destination's fuel tank. If it carried methane, it keeps as much of it as the return flight needs.
The return flight is empty. Whatever found no room at the destination, it brings back.
If the fuel at the destination is not enough for the return flight, the rocket stays there and tries again every 1,200 t (60 s). Store some methane at the destination.

The <item:infinite_horizon:heavy_freighter> carries twice as much. It needs no methane: one <item:infinite_horizon:fuel_rod> lasts for 10 round trips. When it is empty, it takes a fuel rod from its terminal's storage by itself before launching. An atomic drive is already installed.
infinite_horizon.handbook.phase_6.handel: At the <item:infinite_horizon:trading_post> you offer other players trades: "Give me X, you get Y". It has up to 8 offers and its own storage with 54 slots. **Anyone** may trade, including players of other agencies. Only the members of your agency manage storage and offers.
Set up the trading post and open it with a right-click. The offers are on the left, the storage on the right.
Put the goods you want to give away into the storage.
In an offer row, click the **left** pattern slot with an item: that is X, what the trader gives you. A left-click takes the whole stack, a right-click counts up by one.
Click the **right** pattern slot the same way: that is Y, what the trader gets for it.
A left-click without an item clears a pattern slot, a right-click without an item counts down by one.
The patterns are only templates. Trades always use real goods from the storage: next to every offer it says how many more times it works.
What traders give you lands in the storage. Collect it regularly, otherwise the storage fills up at some point and nobody can trade any more.

Put X into your inventory and click "Trade" next to the offer. The trading post takes X from your inventory, puts it into the storage and gives you Y. Players of other agencies do not see the storage, only the offers.

Cargo rockets of your agency and your [[infinite_horizon:reference/agentur|partners]] can choose the trading post as a destination at the [[infinite_horizon:phase_6/logistik_computer|logistics computer]]. They only unload items. Fluids stay in the rocket and fly back.
A trading post is never the start of a route. It has no hangar and no fuel tank: plan the return flight with enough fuel from the start terminal.
infinite_horizon.handbook.phase_6.kernre: The fission reactor supplies 4,000 J/t from <item:infinite_horizon:fuel_rod>. One fuel rod lasts 48,000 t (2,400 s). The reactor has 4 slots for fuel rods and takes the next one by itself.
Output
Energy buffer
Tanks
A water pump over a source next to the reactor reliably keeps the coolant tank full.
Crafting
The structure
The reactor is a cube of 5 × 5 × 5 blocks with a hollow interior, built like the [[infinite_horizon:phase_4/fusionsreaktor|fusion reactor]].
Place the controller (<item:infinite_horizon:fission_reactor>). Its front faces you.
The controller is the **middle of one side face**: the cube extends two blocks left, right, up and down from it and four blocks back.
Build the shell from <item:infinite_horizon:fission_casing>. The interior of 3 × 3 × 3 blocks stays air.
Replace single casing blocks with **ports** where pipes and cables should connect.
As soon as everything is right, the status lamp turns from red to yellow.
**Sneak-right-click** the controller with an empty hand to see red particles where blocks are still missing.
Cooling and heat

While the reactor works, it needs 50 mB of water **or** 5 mB of liquid nitrogen per tick in the coolant tank. Heat changes by -5 per tick with cooling and by 2 without. The progress bar in the window shows the heat.
From 800 it warns with a tone, and the status lamp flashes.
At 1,000 it shuts itself down. It does not explode, but within 16 blocks there is level 3 radiation for 72,000 t (3,600 s).
As soon as the heat is back below 200, it restarts by itself.
After an emergency shutdown you need a suit with a radiation shield or a tier 3 dome for the radiation zone. Without protection you take damage there.
The Fission Reactor
infinite_horizon.handbook.phase_6.logist: At the <item:infinite_horizon:logistics_computer> you set up routes for your [[infinite_horizon:phase_6/frachtraketen|cargo rockets]]. The routes belong to your agency: every logistics computer shows the same ones, no matter where it stands.
Setting up a route
A red line warns you if the outbound and return flights together need more fuel than fits into the tank, and no methane is stored at the destination. The rocket then stays stuck at the destination.
If an outpost is not loaded right now, the logistics computer only checks it every now and then. In doing so it calculates what the producers extracted in the meantime.
Crafting
Set up at least two [[infinite_horizon:phase_6/aussenposten|cargo terminals]] and put a cargo rocket into a hangar slot of the start terminal.
Click "New" at the logistics computer.
Choose start and destination with the buttons. The start is always the terminal whose hangar holds the rocket.
Choose the launch condition and enter N (and X if needed).
Enter the cargo: item or fluid IDs separated by commas. The "Hand" button adds the item in your hand. Empty means: everything.
Under "Rockets", choose the hangar slots whose rockets fly this route. A rocket always belongs to only one route.
Click "Save".
Destinations at partners

Your [[infinite_horizon:phase_6/handelsposten|trading posts]] are also available as destinations and, prefixed with "Partner", the released terminals, shipyards and trading posts of your [[infinite_horizon:reference/agentur|partners]]. If the partnership ends or the partner withdraws the release, the rockets of that route no longer launch. A rocket already on its way brings its cargo back.
