Below the editor you see every rocket of the route: in flight (with time left), loaded (outbound with cargo), waiting or out of fuel. A rocket out of fuel tries again every 1,200 t (60 s).
Logistics Computer
infinite_horizon.handbook.phase_6.sterne: Once the eighth section of the [[infinite_horizon:phase_6/werft|orbital shipyard]] is finished, all members of your agency currently in Earth orbit are told. The "Launch" button then appears at the shipyard terminal.

Clicking "Launch" launches the starship. All members of your agency in Earth orbit see the journey: one after another the planets you have visited pass by, and at the end the Sun stays behind as a small dot. Then the transmitter on [[infinite_horizon:phase_5/pluto|Pluto]] answers, and the credits roll. You can cancel at any time with Esc.
All members of your agency get the advancement "Infinite Horizon". Anyone not in the game right now gets it at their next login.
Visit as many planets as possible with your agency beforehand. Every visited planet appears in the launch sequence.
After the launch, the starship floats next to your station. It has 8 seats, 4 of them for the crew. Right-clicking seats you in a free place. Whoever gets in first belongs to the crew.

With the inventory key the crew chooses a jump destination. The starship only jumps between orbits; you continue to the planets with the [[infinite_horizon:phase_4/landefaehre|lander]]. It needs no fuel: every jump costs 1 filled antimatter cell from your inventory. All passengers jump along.
Empty antimatter cells are not enough. Charge them beforehand in the magnetic trap in Jupiter orbit.
Your starship takes shape in the orbital shipyard. It needs huge amounts of material from every corner of the solar system, so you supply it with [[infinite_horizon:phase_6/frachtraketen|cargo rockets]].
The terminal shows all eight sections with progress bars. Hover over a bar to see what is still missing. The shipyard accepts deliveries for all open sections, the earliest first.
After the eighth section the "Launch" button appears at the terminal ([[infinite_horizon:phase_6/sternenschiff|Launch and Starship]]).

Once a section is fully supplied, the shipyard builds it in 48,000 t (2,400 s). Sections are built in order, from 1 to 8, and the time keeps running even when you are not nearby. With every finished section the scaffold above the terminal grows.
fission reactor, lithium batteries, fuel rods
dome generator III, oxygen generators, greenhouse, clone chamber
Put the <item:infinite_horizon:shipyard_terminal> into the station, at most 48 blocks from the station core. It cannot be placed anywhere else.
Put at least one <item:infinite_horizon:shipyard_dock> into the same station. It is the landing target of your cargo rockets.
Without a shipyard dock in the station, the shipyard cannot accept anything. The terminal then shows a red notice.

Whatever arrives at the dock moves straight into the shipyard store. The store is unlimited, but only takes what the shipyard still needs. Everything else stays in the rocket and flies back. Pipes and hoppers at the dock deliver too.
Methane first fills the dock's fuel tank. Your rockets refuel from it for the return flight. Only the rest goes into the shipyard store.
For the flight computer, the shipyard only accepts a star chart of your own agency.

At the [[infinite_horizon:phase_6/logistik_computer|logistics computer]], set up routes with the condition "until demand is met" to the dock. The rockets then only load what the shipyard still needs and stop by themselves.

The "Partners" button in the shipyard GUI releases the shipyard for your [[infinite_horizon:reference/agentur|partners]]. Their cargo rockets may then supply the docks. Every agency that delivered at least one item or fluid also gets the advancement when the starship launches.
infinite_horizon.handbook.reference.agen: Every player belongs to an **agency**. It is your space program: all members share research points and research, later also atlas, routes and stations. If you play alone, you are your own agency.
How it comes about
If the leader leaves, the engineer who has been there longest becomes leader.
Whoever joins another agency does not take their research points and research along. The new agency's progress applies.
Rights
Role
May
Leader
everything, plus invite, assign roles, rename and form partnerships
Engineer
build, operate and configure machines, research, launch rockets, change routes
Guest
open and view the agency's machines and containers, but take out, put in, configure or break nothing
Non-member
like a guest, at other agencies
**Dome protection:** in an active dome of another agency, non-members place and break no blocks, not even dirt or stone. Anyone may breathe there.
Server **operators** are exempt from these rules, as with spawn protection.
Roles and name
The leader manages the agency in the **Agency** tab:
**Change role:** next to every member is a button with their role. One click switches between engineer and guest. The member gets a message.
**Hand over leadership:** the "Leader" button makes the member leader. You yourself then become an engineer.
**Rename:** enter a name at the bottom left and click "Rename". An empty name restores "<founder>'s Agency".
Give players who should only watch the guest role. Then they cannot break anything by accident.
Partners

When you enter the world, the server checks whether you belong to an agency. If not, it founds one for you, and you are its **leader**. That also applies to worlds that existed before this version. As long as the agency has no name of its own, it is called "<your name>'s Agency".

Two agencies can become **partners**. Their cargo rockets may then supply each other: released [[infinite_horizon:phase_6/aussenposten|cargo terminals]], released [[infinite_horizon:phase_6/werft|shipyards]] and every [[infinite_horizon:phase_6/handelsposten|trading post]].
The leader opens the **Partners** tab at the <item:infinite_horizon:research_terminal>. On the right are the agencies with someone online right now.
They click "Offer" next to an agency. Its members get a message.
The leader of the other agency sees the offer on the left under "Offers to you" and clicks "Accept".
The partnership only applies once both leaders have confirmed. Either leader can dissolve it again with "End".
Partners are not members: in other agencies' domes and at their machines they still only have guest rights.
You decide yourself what a partner may supply: at the cargo terminal and the shipyard, the "Partners" button switches the release on or off. Trading posts are always open to partners.
Commands
`/infinite_horizon agency info` shows your agency: name, ID, members with role and visited dimensions. With a player name after it, it shows that player's agency.

`/infinite_horizon agency transfer <from> <to>` (operators only): all property of the first agency passes to the second. Instead of an agency ID you may give a player name. The old agency loses its members. If one comes back, they get a new agency.

If someone no longer plays on the server, an operator can give their machines to another agency with `transfer`. The blocks change owner by themselves at the next access; you do not have to place anything again.
`transfer` cannot be undone: the old agency is empty afterwards, and its property belongs to the new one for good.

The agency also remembers every dimension one of its members has entered. That counts for research: when a member sets foot on the Moon, tier 2 opens (see [[infinite_horizon:phase_2/forschung|Research]]).
Ownership
If you place a machine, a generator, a storage block or a port, it belongs to your agency. Cables, pipes and casing blocks have no owner.
Blocks not placed by a player (by command, from a dispenser or from older worlds) have **no owner**. Anyone may use them. Whoever opens their GUI first becomes their owner with their agency.
Joining and leaving
Everything happens at the <item:infinite_horizon:research_terminal> in the **Agency** tab. There you see the members with their roles.
**Invite:** the leader sees on the right all players who are online and not members, and invites them with a button. The invited player gets a chat message.
**Accept or decline:** your open invitations are at the bottom right. You can accept at **any** research terminal, even someone else's.

**Joining:** you leave your old agency and become an engineer of the new one. If the old one becomes empty, all its property (machines, domes, terminals) belongs to the new one from then on. Research points and research of the old agency are **not** transferred.
**Leaving:** you immediately found a new agency of your own and are its leader. You cannot leave if you are alone.
Your Agency
infinite_horizon.handbook.reference.erfo: The Infinite Horizon advancements are on their own tab in the advancements menu (key `L`). They trace the journey from the first research terminal to the launch of the starship.
Defeat the sentinel at the transmitter.
5 routes of your agency are active at the same time: each has at least one rocket, and none of them reports "out of fuel".
A probe of your agency reaches the Moon.
Descend below the cloud layer on Venus (below y 180) and make it back up.
A dome generator of your agency runs for the first time.
fusion reactor]] of your agency generates power.
Dive below the ice shell into the water on Europa.

Advancements triggered by a machine or an event go to **all members** of your agency: First Signal, Air of Your Own, Sun in a Bottle, Network and the starship. Whoever is not online right now gets them the next time they enter the world.
When the starship launches, all [[infinite_horizon:reference/agentur|partner]] agencies that delivered something to the shipyard get the advancement too.
The server writes every advancement with time and player name into the file `logs/infinite_horizon-progress.log`. It stays on the server and is not sent anywhere.
infinite_horizon.handbook.reference.item: All items, blocks and fluids of the current version. Clicking a name takes you to the page that explains it.
infinite_horizon.handbook.reference.reze: Here are all recipes of the current version. The values come straight from the mod's data. Time and energy apply without [[infinite_horizon:phase_1/upgrades|upgrades]].
Servers can change recipe amounts with the `recipe_amount_multiplier` setting. The assembly table then uses different amounts than shown here.
infinite_horizon.handbook.reference.tipp: **Crush first, then smelt.** That doubles every metal.
**Keep a stock of machine frames.** Almost every machine needs one.
**Keep titanium in mind.** Rockets eat titanium plates. Remember good spots deep underground.
**Plan the refinery early.** Without plastic there are no circuits, and without circuits you cannot go to space.
**One network, one purpose.** Separate pipes for water and crude oil save you a lot of searching.
Almost all numbers (consumption, time, throughput) are in data packs under `data/<namespace>/infinite_horizon/balance/` and can be changed with `/reload`.
`serverconfig/infinite_horizon.json` lets you set, among other things, recipe amounts, oxygen consumption and events.
**The lamp is yellow and nothing happens.** The machine is waiting for material or power. Check whether the energy bar is empty and whether the input matches a recipe.
**The lamp is red.** The output is full, or a block is missing in the refinery. Hover over the lamp in the window; it shows the reason.
**The assembly table does not start.** It needs the ingredients in exactly the right amount. Take out the surplus. See [[infinite_horizon:phase_1/montagetisch|Assembly Table]].
**The pipe transports nothing.** A pipe network carries only one fluid. If another one is still inside, it waits until the network is empty. Also check the output side of the source ("Side" button).
**My machines run slowly although the generator is full.** A copper cable carries only 256 J/t. If too many machines hang on one network, split it.
**I cannot find titanium.** Titanium lies below y 0. Without an iron pickaxe the ore drops nothing.
**I cannot find crude oil.** Oil pockets only exist under deserts and oceans. Explore caves in those biomes. See [[infinite_horizon:phase_1/rohstoffe|Resources and Ores]].
infinite_horizon.handbook.start.bedienun: All Infinite Horizon machines follow the same rules. Once you understand them, you can handle every new machine right away.
The window
Break machines with a **pickaxe** (stone or better). They drop themselves, and items inside fall out. Energy and fluids are lost. Only the <item:infinite_horizon:fluid_tank> keeps its contents.
A machine uses power only while it is actually working. A waiting machine costs nothing, so feel free to hook several machines to one generator.
Right-clicking a machine opens its window:
**Far left** the energy bar: how much power the machine has stored.
**Left** the input slots, **right** the output slots, the progress arrow in between.
**Far right** the fluid bars, if the machine has tanks. Below them are the fill and drain slots for buckets.
**Bottom right** the two upgrade slots (see [[infinite_horizon:phase_1/upgrades|Upgrades]]).
The **"Side"** button chooses on which side the machine outputs fluids. With several output tanks, the **"Tank"** button chooses which one fills the bucket.
The status lamp
Every machine has a small lamp on top. It tells you at a glance what is going on:
**Green** – the machine is working.
**Yellow** – it is waiting for material or power.
**Red** – something is wrong: the output is full, the machine stands in the wrong place or a structure is incomplete. Hover over the lamp in the window to see the reason.
Automating with hoppers and pipes
Items and fluids enter the input **from every side**. Hoppers always fill the first matching slot.
From every side you can extract **only the results**. That makes chaining machines easy.
A machine outputs fluids only through its **output side** (button "Side"). That side accepts nothing itself, so nothing flows back into the pipe that feeds the machine.
Shift-clicking in the window puts upgrades into the upgrade slots and molds into the mold slot, everything else into the input.
Breaking
Using Machines
infinite_horizon.handbook.start.grundbeg: This page explains the few terms that appear all over the handbook. You need nothing more to get started.
Ticks and seconds
**Green:** working.
**Yellow:** waiting for material or power.
**Red:** problem. The output is full, a structure is incomplete or the machine stands in the wrong place. In the window, the lamp's tooltip tells you the reason.
Inputs and outputs
Machines accept items and fluids **from all sides**. You can connect hoppers and pipes wherever you like.
Machines and storage blocks output fluids and stored power through **one side** only, the **output side**. You choose it in the window with the "Side" button.
Multiblocks

Some machines are so big that they consist of many blocks, for example the [[infinite_horizon:phase_1/raffinerie|Refinery]]. You place a **controller** and build the given shape around it from **casing blocks**. **Ports** replace single casing blocks and are the connections for pipes, cables and hoppers.
Phases

Infinite Horizon is split into six **phases**, from industry on Earth to the starship. Each phase has its own chapter in the handbook with a "First Steps" page. From phase 2 on, you unlock new technology through **research**.
If you remember only one thing: **green works, yellow waits, red has a problem.** One look at the lamps shows you where your factory is stuck.
Minecraft counts in **ticks (t)**. One second has 20 ticks. If a machine needs "200 t (10 s)", one operation takes ten seconds.
Power: J and J/t
Power is measured in **joules (J)**.
**J/t** means "joules per tick". A generator with 20 J/t produces 20 J every tick; a machine with 20 J/t uses that much while it works.
Power flows through **cables** from generators to machines. Every cable has a **throughput**: the most J/t it can carry.
Every machine has a small **buffer**. If power is short for a moment, it pauses and then carries on. Nothing is lost.
More under [[infinite_horizon:phase_1/strom|Power]].
Fluids: mB

Liquids and gases are called **fluids**. They are measured in **millibuckets (mB)**: 1,000 mB are exactly one bucket. Fluids travel through **pipes** and are stored in **tanks**. More under [[infinite_horizon:phase_1/fluide|Fluids and Pipes]].
The status lamp
Every machine has a small lamp:
Basics
infinite_horizon.handbook.start.umwelt.e: On Earth you never have to think about air, pressure or temperature. On other worlds you do: every world has its own **environment values**, and every hazard you are not protected against builds up **strain**.
The environment values

Once the hazard is gone, the strain drops back to 0 in 100 t (5 s). Several hazards count separately: without a suit on the Moon, oxygen and pressure rise at the same time, plus heat or cold depending on the time of day.
In creative and spectator mode there is no strain. After death it starts at 0 again.
Strain gives you only a short warning: after 200 t (10 s) in a vacuum the damage begins. Never go outside without a plan.
The HUD display
Above the hunger bar, each hazard gets its own bar as soon as its strain rises. It is green, turns yellow from 50 % and red from 80 %. A warning tone sounds when it appears.

If you wear a complete [[infinite_horizon:phase_2/raumanzug|pressure suit]] outside breathable air, another bar shows its oxygen supply. If temperature or radiation lie outside what you can bear without a suit, their values are shown above.
Gravity

Every world has its own gravity. On the Moon it is 0.17 times Earth's. You fall more slowly, jump much higher and survive deep falls without damage: the safe fall height (3 blocks on Earth) is divided by the gravity, and fall damage shrinks by the same amount.
The jump strength itself stays the same. That is why you jump many times higher on the Moon than on Earth.
Radiation can be shielded: just 3 solid blocks overhead lower it by 2 levels. On alien worlds, a cave or a roof is often the quickest cover.
Every 10 t (0.5 s) the server checks where you stand and works out:
**Breathable air:** Is there a breathable atmosphere? Not on the Moon.
**Temperature:** It follows daylight. On the Moon it rises to 120 °C at noon and drops to -170 °C at night. At dusk and dawn it lies in between.
**Pressure:** from vacuum through low and normal to high.
**Radiation:** level 0 to 3. With at least 3 solid blocks above you, it drops by 2 levels.
Some areas have their own values. In the Moon's polar crater it always stays at -190 °C, and there is no solar power there.
Dimensions without their own environment values, such as the Nether, the End or worlds from other mods, count as Earth.

infinite_horizon.handbook.start.willkomm: Welcome, engineer! You stand at the start of a long journey: from a small workshop on Earth to the **orbital shipyard**, where you finally build the starship.

Infinite Horizon takes you through the **real solar system**. Every step builds on the one before: first you need power and machines, then fuel, then a rocket. On the Moon you learn to survive without air, on Venus to brave the heat, and far out near Pluto a signal is waiting that nobody can explain.

The <item:infinite_horizon:planetary_atlas> later collects what you find out about the planets. You get it on your first login; right-click opens it. See [[infinite_horizon:phase_2/atlas|The Planetary Atlas]].
Start with [[infinite_horizon:phase_1/erste_schritte|First Steps]]. It walks you through the whole first phase step by step.
The journey in six phases
**Earth industry** – ores, power, machines, crude oil and plastic.
**Space program** – research, the first probe, the first rocket, the Moon.
**Ring 1** – Moon, Mars and Venus, space suit and domes.
**Orbit** – your own space station and fusion power.
**Ring 2** – from Mercury to Pluto, with ever harsher conditions.
**Network and finale** – cargo rockets between your outposts and the starship.
How to use this handbook
The handbook grows with you: a new chapter opens as soon as you reach the matching research tier.
Underlined terms are **links**. One click takes you to the matching page.
Recipes are shown right on the machine pages. You find an overview under [[infinite_horizon:reference/rezepte|All Recipes]].
New to Infinite Horizon? Read the [[infinite_horizon:start/grundbegriffe|Basics]] first.
Stuck? Look at [[infinite_horizon:phase_1/erste_schritte|First Steps]] or the [[infinite_horizon:reference/tipps|Tips and FAQ]].
Handbook and atlas

You get the <item:infinite_horizon:engineers_handbook> when you first enter the world. Right-click opens it. Hover over an item in your inventory and press **H**, and the handbook jumps to that item's page. Lost it? You can craft a new one at the crafting table.
